slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jog the reservoir
slots.text: Run the 1.58-mile loop around the Jackie O Reservoir like a local, pausing at the overlooks for city views and resident herons.
slots.food: Breakfast at Breads Bakery: chocolate babka and rugelach to go.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Get lost at The Frick
slots.text: Head for the newly reopened Frick Collection, a Gilded Age mansion strong in Old Masters and European sculpture. Just over an hour.
slots.food: Lunch at Café Sabarsky: goulash soup or schnitzel, then Sacher torte.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Check out a jazz show
slots.venue: The Jazz Club at Aman New York
slots.text: Come for the jazz, from Grammy-winning bassists to powerhouse vocalists, and stay for the chic atmosphere and DJ set.
slots.food: Dinner at Chez FiFi: French fare in a mahogany-paneled townhouse; book early.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Stroll the Village
slots.text: Walking the West Village on a sunny spring day is pure ambrosia. Lose yourself on Commerce Street and visit Stonewall.
slots.food: Breakfast at Café Cluny: grapefruit brûlée and a French omelet.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Three Lives & Company
slots.text: Spend an hour in this indie bookstore, a neighbourhood touchstone with a great travel-book section. Left Bank Books is nearby.
slots.food: Lunch at Moustache Pitza: paper-thin pita with dips and grilled meats.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails and comedy
slots.text: Start with a cocktail at Little Branch, a 1920s-style bar behind an unmarked door, then catch the Comedy Cellar or the Village Vanguard.
slots.food: Late-night: a folded slice at Joe's Pizza, the real nightcap.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Souvenir shopping
slots.text: Walk up Court and Smith Streets for indie fashion and cafés. Emma Straub's Books Are Magic could take up the whole morning.
slots.food: Breakfast at Court Street Grocers: eggs and cheddar on ciabatta.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A flick in Cobble Hill
slots.text: Catch an impromptu movie at this neighbourhood joint, which opened in the 1920s as the Lido. Bring a spicy hot chocolate from next door.
slots.food: Lunch: Caputo's cold cuts and Monteleone cannoli for Carroll Park.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dancing at Public Records
slots.text: Technically in Gowanus, this repurposed warehouse holds a hi-fi listening bar, a vegan café by day and a nightclub.
slots.food: Dinner at Frankies Spuntino: the crowd-favourite ravioli in the garden.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Yoga (or Pilates)
slots.text: Anchor the trip with a workout: Wild Thing's heated yoga class is always a push in the best way.
slots.food: Breakfast at Facade Bakery: cornflake matcha, olive oil cake and perfectly executed egg dishes.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A walk around Coconut Grove
slots.text: Spend the afternoon on a walk around Coconut Grove.
slots.food: Lunch at Krüs Kitchen: farm-to-table fare upstairs from Michelin-starred Los Félix, by the same chef.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nightcaps with a side of vinyl
slots.text: A vinyl lounge just upstairs from Fooq's, with low ceilings, Persian rugs, brass accents and only a handful of tables.
slots.food: Dinner at Fooq's: shareable plates with Persian and Mediterranean influences.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sweat session, then the beach
slots.text: Heated Pilates at Tondo Room, then straight to the wide, clean beach at The Ritz-Carlton, Key Biscayne.
slots.food: Breakfast at Flour & Weirdoughs: croissants that shatter when you bite into them.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Rubell Museum
slots.text: One of the largest private collections of contemporary art in North America, collected early in the artists' careers.
slots.food: Lunch at Gramps Getaway: Florida Keys shack energy and cold drinks in plastic cups.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Live music at Zey Zey
slots.text: An open-air cultural space, part live music venue, part food hall, with a lineup of artists who usually skip Miami.
slots.food: Dinner at Sunny's Steakhouse: steak, pasta and house rolls under a massive tree.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Design District, Little River
slots.text: A morning in the Design District and Little River.
slots.food: Breakfast at Under the Mango Tree: smoothies, açaí bowls and juices at a Miami classic.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Spa time at The Standard
slots.text: Cycle between the hammam, sauna and ice room, then sit by the pool over the bay. Drinks at Lido Bayside Grill at golden hour.
slots.food: Lunch at Vecinos: burgers and natural wine at a spot where nothing is trying too hard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dancing at Medium Cool
slots.text: A little moody, perfect for energy without the chaos. A small, packed room where you'll be dancing, with vinyl nights.
slots.food: Dinner at Palma: a seasonal tasting menu in an intimate, cozy space.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A Day in Sants food tour
slots.text: Culinary Backstreets' Feasting Off the Grid tour: intimate, run by food writers who know the restaurants personally.
slots.food: Breakfast, morning and lunch all come on the tour, which eats up most of the day.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rest before dinner
slots.text: The tour eats up most of the day. A nap afterwards is highly recommended before dinner at Lluritu.
slots.food: Lunch is on the tour too, so come hungry.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A flamenco performance
slots.text: End the night with a flamenco performance.
slots.food: Dinner at Lluritu: seafood cooked brilliantly; get the huevos rotos con gambas al ajillo.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Take in some art
slots.text: Set aside a couple of hours for VASTO Gallery, the most beautiful in Barcelona, with incredible openings and events.
slots.food: Breakfast at ETL: Mexican fare modernised beautifully; everything with corn is divine.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: More art at La Fabra
slots.text: Explore more contemporary, less mainstream artistic voices at La Fabra, whose current exhibition is potent and relevant.
slots.food: Lunch at Achaar Bar: one of the most delicious dahls of your life.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Live music at La Paloma
slots.text: On a Sunday from 6 to 9 p.m., join all ages dancing to Latin music, especially salsa, in a century-old ballroom.
slots.food: Dinner at Entrepreneur: classic Catalan, with historic architecture and green velvet seats.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A dose of culture
slots.text: Start the day with a dose of culture.
slots.food: Breakfast at Hotel Brummel: baked goods on the inner patio where creatives gather.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A sunset catamaran cruise
slots.text: Catch a Barcelona sunset at sea, with live music. Easy to book as a group or solo, or go by paddleboard.
slots.food: Lunch at Osteria Borbotta: Tuscan homemade pasta stretched right in front of you.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Movie night at Zumzeig
slots.text: A neighbourhood cinema with one room showing one film at a time: precious, rare films from all over the world.
slots.food: Dinner at Denassus: classic Catalan, a modern fusion with Spanish tradition.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A photo walk through Kastellet
slots.text: One of the most beautiful and peaceful places in town, especially at the start and end of the day when there are fewer tourists.
slots.food: Breakfast at Atelier September: the open-face avocado on rye and the omelette.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A dose of art and design
slots.text: Spend the afternoon with a dose of art and design.
slots.food: Lunch at Bottega Barlie: sourdough with olive oil, the omelette and everything with fish.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Tivoli time
slots.text: Even more magical when the sun and crowds go away: at night there's breathing room to take everything in at your own pace.
slots.food: Dinner at Vinoria Lilo: the three-course menu, with natural wine and candlelight.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dive into Inner City
slots.text: Dive into the Inner City.
slots.food: Breakfast at Café Beau Marché: Parisian-inspired fare in a photogenic backyard.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A quick dip at Nordhavn
slots.text: Modern and industrial. Do as the Danes do: jump in the water, then heat up in the sauna at Sauna House.
slots.food: Lunch at Louise Roe Bar and Gallery: eat off the brand's own plates and glasses.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails at Ruby
slots.text: A hidden gem towards the canals, where stepping inside feels like entering another time, with world-class cocktails.
slots.food: Dinner at Bobe: chef Bo Bech's restaurant, cozy with no hint of pretension.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
slots.text: Take the train to Humlebæk and walk to this modernistic architectural masterpiece, guaranteed to leave an impression.
slots.food: Breakfast at Wulff & Konstali: pastries near the shore at Klampenborg.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Unwind in King's Garden
slots.text: Back in the city, take a break in one of the author's favourite parks, or visit the Palm House if it rains.
slots.food: Lunch at the Louisiana Café: ocean views outside, a crackling fireplace inside.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A magical bridge crossing
slots.text: At its most magical after dark. Walk the quiet canals and old lanterns, and cross the bridge at the end of Nyhavn.
slots.food: Dinner at Esmée: a menu that makes you wish you could have it all, with views.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A walk along the River Tagus
slots.venue: Pousada de Lisboa, Praça do Comércio
slots.text: Avoid the afternoon crowds and stroll the river early, from Praça do Comércio as far as your legs will take you.
slots.food: Breakfast at Heim Café: the savory French toast with green sauce.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Wander Monsanto Forest Park
slots.text: Lisbon's national forest is the city's largest green space, with eucalyptus trees that smell incredible.
slots.food: Lunch at Imperial de Campo de Ourique: a traditional tasca; opt for the menu do dia.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A sunset river cruise
slots.text: Seeing Lisbon from the water is special, especially on a warm summer evening. Then follow the energy into Bairro Alto.
slots.food: Dinner at Pigmeu: an entire menu of nose-to-tail pork in Portuguese tradition.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Port tasting
slots.text: Charming sommeliers talk you through tawny, ruby and white ports until you're debating how many bottles fit in your suitcase.
slots.food: Breakfast at Neighbourhood: breakfast burritos worth the line.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A stroll around Alfama
slots.text: The old town of cobblestone roads, terracotta roofs and hidden gems, from family-run tascas to São Jorge Castle's views.
slots.food: Lunch at As Bifanas do Afonso: a hole-in-the-wall that does one dish, a pork bifana.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A fado show
slots.text: Fado drifts through Alfama each evening. Mesa de Frades is where fado singers go for inspiration.
slots.food: Dinner at O Velho Eurico: share the whole menu, and never skip the bacalhau à brás.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Belém Tower views
slots.venue: Belém Tower (Torre de Belém / Torre de São Vicente)
slots.text: A 16th-century fortress and UNESCO site, fascinating up close. The nearby Jerónimos Monastery is a great follow-up.
slots.food: Breakfast at Do Beco: a padaria always doing something new, like a matcha choux bun.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A sand session
slots.text: A 16-mile stretch of soft white sand, with locals escaping the city and endless cafés serving fresh fish and salads.
slots.food: Lunch at Pastéis de Belém: decide whether it beats the pastel de nata.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sunset from a miradouro
slots.venue: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
slots.text: Often a late-night party or food market. Grab a cold Super Bock from the kiosk as the sun goes down.
slots.food: Dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro: garlicky prawns, fresh fish and fat lobsters, shoulder to shoulder.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A wander through Hyde Park
slots.text: One of London's largest green spaces, perfect in any season and a jewel box of browns, reds and golds in autumn.
slots.food: Breakfast at Mount Street Restaurant: British classics among works by Warhol and Matisse.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Wallace Collection
slots.text: Avoid the crowds and see something different at this Manchester Square gallery, a great way to spend an afternoon.
slots.food: Lunch at Arôme Bakery: honey butter toast at a French-Asian bakery on Duke Street.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Live music at Ronnie Scott's
slots.text: A legendary jazz club with world-class live music every night since 1959. Book ahead and order a Manhattan.
slots.food: Dinner at The Hart: elevated pub fare; don't leave without the banoffee pie.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Souvenirs at Broadway Market
slots.text: Stallholders fill the street at weekends. Try Pavilion Bakery, Donlon Books for browsing and Climpson & Son's for coffee.
slots.food: Breakfast at Bistrotheque: the pork Benedict in a white-washed, exposed-brick space.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Hackney City Farm
slots.text: Yes, really, a farm in the middle of the city. Visit ponies, donkeys, sheep and goats, or wander the orchard.
slots.food: Lunch at Deeneys: the Macbeth toastie of spiced lamb, caramelised onions and cheddar.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nightcaps at Satan's Whiskers
slots.text: Down-to-earth service, a fuss-free menu and lip-smackingly good cocktails; number 21 on The World's 50 Best Bars.
slots.food: Dinner at Cafe Cecilia: super seasonal dishes at a canal-front hangout; book ahead.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Brick Lane stalls and snacks
slots.text: Few places are as full of life: stalls selling just about anything and food carts covering every cuisine imaginable.
slots.food: Breakfast at Jolene Redchurch Street: coffee and pastries worth the line around the corner.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sauna & Plunge
slots.text: Inspired by the Scandinavian fjords: a 30-minute sauna and five-minute ice bath without breaking the bank.
slots.food: Lunch at Beigel Bake: chewy bagels with juicy salt beef, beloved by every Londoner.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Karaoke at Bao Shoreditch
slots.text: The only thing better than karaoke is karaoke that comes with a side of dumplings.
slots.food: Dinner at Singburi: fiery beef larb, ginger chicken thighs and tiger prawn curry.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Walk through Los Rosales
slots.text: Stop at the Temple of Debod, an Egyptian temple from the 2nd century BC, and the Royal Palace, with unbeatable views.
slots.food: Breakfast at Alma Nomad Bakery: a ham and cheese croissant that becomes something delicious.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Shop Contemporánea Condeduque
slots.text: Some favourite men's stores call this neighbourhood home, including Sportivo, Mini Shop and La Compañía Polar.
slots.food: Lunch at El Pedrusco: the best traditional cuisine, cooked in a wood-fired oven.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Two vibes, multiple cocktails
slots.text: Start at Kinki, a tiny, super-modern bar, then Moloko Sound Club, an indie temple playing the best of the '80s and '90s.
slots.food: Dinner at Amis: shareable dishes and wines from around the world.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Embrace the chaos at El Rastro
slots.text: Visit the antique shops on Saturdays, when crowds are more manageable, then stop at Casa Amadeo for snails.
slots.food: Breakfast at La Duquesita: the best chocolate palmeras in the world; show up early.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Soak in Gran Vía
slots.text: Always crowded but worth seeing: Madrid's most iconic street, with neon lights, sprawling stores and historic theaters.
slots.food: Lunch at La Tasquita de Enfrente: market-fresh fare, chef Ferran Adrià's favourite.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Salesas Chueca
slots.text: Great new cocktail bars like Ficus and Jack's Library, and historic nightlife temples Del Diego and Bar Cock.
slots.food: Dinner at La Llorería: so many dishes from such a small place; book ahead.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza
slots.text: Both temporary exhibitions and the collection make it one of the best museums in the world. Don't forget the shop.
slots.food: Breakfast at Estela Hojaldre: the best puff pastry in Madrid.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Go gallery hopping
slots.text: Choose Huertas or Lavapiés, or head to Carabanchel, the new art district, for emerging artists and galleries.
slots.food: Lunch at El Jardín del Ritz: authentic Valencian paella and addictive chicken skewers.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Experience Spanish Broadway
slots.text: Madrid is said to be the Spanish Broadway, with countless musicals. For classics, try the Teatro Español.
slots.food: Dinner at Corral de la Morería: the best sherry cellar, a Michelin-starred menu and flamenco.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Stroll Lomas
slots.text: Start the day with a stroll around Lomas.
slots.food: Breakfast at Chiquitito: a light breakfast, good coffee and a nice book selection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Wander the Botanical Garden
slots.text: Walk through Chapultepec's botanical garden to Lago Algo, a gallery and restaurant in a modernist building. Order a carajillo.
slots.food: Lunch at La Once Mil: a tiny taquería; try the black angus trompo taco.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Drinks at Pistilo
slots.text: A relatively new spot with great drinks, like the Piña-Chaya cocktail, and a really good ambience.
slots.food: Dinner at MO+F: a broad take on Asian cuisine; try the Tom Yam ramen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Art and design at Casa Basalta
slots.text: A Porfirian-era house turned creative hub. Spend a couple of hours across levels, with MAIA Contemporary for emerging art.
slots.food: Breakfast at Lardo: green chilaquiles with sunny side up eggs, and a guayaba roll.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Art spotting at Mooni Gallery
slots.text: The whole block is curated by the same team: a mix of art, objects and clothes from Latin American creators.
slots.food: Lunch at El Jamil: Lebanese food among greenery and tiles, tucked away from the chaos.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Wine at Fantasma
slots.text: After dinner, go next door for good wine, good music and an easy vibe: just sit and talk before heading back.
slots.food: Dinner at Fugaz: a small, well-executed menu where locals go with good friends.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A self-guided mural tour
slots.text: The courtyard of the SEP is packed with Diego Rivera murals, and far less crowded than the typical tourist stops.
slots.food: Breakfast at Blom: a flat white and a torta de aguacate, requesón y arúgula.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Padel and a drink
slots.text: An outdoor padel club that's become a social hub: book a match, or grab a beer on the terrace and watch.
slots.food: Lunch at Las Tlayudas: the veggie tlayuda, with tetelas and guacamole.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A nightcap (or two)
slots.text: The plaza is always alive. Order the Ritual cocktail, made with local herbs, in a famous "haunted" building.
slots.food: Dinner at Órbita: short rib quesabirrias with an exquisite sound system.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A bit of souvenir shopping
slots.text: Start the day with a bit of souvenir shopping in Le Marais.
slots.food: Breakfast at Dreamin' Man: orange-ricotta pancake and a matcha latte from a small Japanese-owned shop.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Vintage shopping
slots.text: Spend the afternoon vintage shopping in Le Marais.
slots.food: Lunch at Recoin: a farmer's market-sourced three-course menu, much loved by locals.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nightcap at Delicatessen Place
slots.text: A welcoming spot with great natural wines by the glass or bottle; try the Alsace wines or anything from the Jura.
slots.food: Dinner at Bistrot des Tournelles: classic French comfort food and a homemade cordon bleu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
slots.text: One of the best places to wander and breathe, with an elevated view of all Paris, in the morning or at sunset.
slots.food: Breakfast at Le Petit Grain: the best croissants in Paris and buckwheat chocolate cookies.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Canal Saint-Martin
slots.text: Get a cone from JJ Hings (sweet corn soft serve, peach sorbet), then stroll the canal up to the 19th arrondissement.
slots.food: Lunch at Le Dauphin: a Basque-influenced menu that changes daily, with a Vermouth cocktail.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails at Combat
slots.text: The perfect way to end the day: about 30 seats, at the counter or in the back. Try the orange blossom, rum and milk drink.
slots.food: Dinner at Cendrillon: bold, acidic, spicy dishes with a punk twist, rare in Paris.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A piece of medieval France
slots.text: Come for one thing: pâté en croûte, a medieval staple and a great souvenir for foodie friends.
slots.food: Breakfast at Wani Coffee Shop: true Japanese matcha with pistachio and chestnut flour cookies.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Astier de Villatte
slots.text: Beautiful handmade ceramics, made in the heart of Paris for 30 years, plus home fragrances and stationery.
slots.food: Lunch at Brasserie Lipp: where Chirac, Sartre and Hemingway ate, served by uniformed garçons.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails at Cravan
slots.text: Low-lit rooms where you'll linger late. A cultural space blending mixology, design and publishing, with its own magazine.
slots.food: Dinner at Orson: Korean fine dining; try the crab tteok-bokki.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Golden souvenirs
slots.text: Gift yourself a piece of antique Rome from a favourite goldsmith's workshop, which pays homage to the city.
slots.food: Breakfast at Forno Campo de' Fiori: pizza rossa for salty, crostatina di visciole for sweet.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A walk through Aventino
slots.text: A peaceful walk past Circo Massimo and the Rose Garden. Stop at Santa Sabina, a 5th-century basilica.
slots.food: Lunch at Cesare al Pellegrino: unfussy Italian fare and excellent produce.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A nightcap (or three)
slots.text: Bottles from lesser-known European vineyards: in the owner's words, "the perfect antidote" to most things.
slots.food: Dinner at Piatto Romano: a veggie-heavy feast of seasonal dishes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A dose of contemporary art
slots.text: An archaeological site within Trajan's Forum turned art space, where 2nd-century structures meet the present.
slots.food: Breakfast at Regoli: legendary maritozzi and crostatine di visciole.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gelato and Caravaggios
slots.text: Stroll to Otaleg or Ciampini for gelato, then see the Caravaggios in the Church of San Luigi dei Francesi.
slots.food: Lunch: classic Roman dishes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Natural wine among locals
slots.text: An oasis for natural wines: a very local, legit space even amid Trastevere's growing "Disneyfication."
slots.food: Dinner at Le Mani in Pasta: a parade of seafood; try the spigola carpaccio with truffle.

days.title: A day trip to Campagnano Romano

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A dip in a volcanic lake
slots.text: Drive 45 minutes to Bracciano Lake. The remarkably clear water is perfect for a swim before exploring Trevignano.
slots.food: Breakfast at Santi Sebastiano e Valentino: pastries and bread for the road.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Italian Art Deco
slots.text: A hidden gem only recently open for private tours: a nearly untouched masterpiece of Italian Art Deco.
slots.food: Lunch at Osteria Iotto: a farm-sourced menu; try the tacos alla picchiapò.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nightcaps at La Mescita
slots.text: Wind down at a bar usually filled with locals. Ask for the natural wines, or go for a low-key aperitivo.
slots.food: Dinner at Trecca: revived forgotten Roman classics; this is the place for offal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Edo-Tokyo Open-Air Museum
slots.text: A hidden gem whose exhibit doubles as a lesson in how the region's historical architecture is preserved.
slots.food: Breakfast at Chiya-Ba: possibly the best chai in town, in a beautiful interior.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Souvenirs at Galerie 21
slots.text: A quiet, appointment-only space in Nakameguro where craft, objects and personal stories come together.
slots.food: Lunch at Curry Bondy: a rich Japanese classic, famous for its cheese curry.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Drinks at Wine and Things
slots.text: A small local wine shop in Nakameguro, perfect for a late-night drink, with an impeccable mix of local and imported wines.
slots.food: Dinner at AC House: ever-changing seasonal dishes from a chef with his own vision.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Japan Folk Craft Museum
slots.text: Celebrates the beauty of everyday handmade objects, with a strong permanent collection and occasional exhibitions.
slots.food: Breakfast at Alley Cats: a canteen in a former 100-yen shop; order the smash burger.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: News reads at Nostos Books
slots.text: A treasure trove of rare, carefully curated art and photography books, perfect if you have nothing specific in mind.
slots.food: Lunch at Suba VS: inventive soba; the lime and fig soba is the favourite.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Natural wine at Takarabune
slots.text: A menu that changes weekly, only four or five tables, and a short menu based on the chef's recommendations.
slots.food: Dinner at Pignon: cozy, French-inspired food with a great wine selection.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Traditional crafts at Casica
slots.text: In Shin Kiba, known for its folkloric craft atmosphere: a good place for local snacks, crafts and special souvenirs.
slots.food: Breakfast at Toraya: anmitsu and yokan for a quiet, sweet morning tea.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rare crafts at Bingoya
slots.text: One of Tokyo's oldest craft stores, with rare crafts from around Japan that are almost impossible to find elsewhere.
slots.food: Lunch at Menya Jojo: the best duck ramen and tsukemen in Kuramae, rich without a nap.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nightcaps at No. 501
slots.text: A carefully curated selection of natural wines in a relaxed atmosphere, easy to stop by and discover something new.
slots.food: Dinner at ADI: a weekly course of Japanese and Nepali flavours; the curry shines.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Broad
slots.text: LA's best modern art museum in the author's book, and a great reason to take yourself downtown.
slots.food: Breakfast at Grand Central Market: chilaquiles, egg sandwiches and pastries, then Angels Flight.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Chinatown shopping and wine
slots.text: Score a mah jong set and vintage, or splurge at KkCo and Eckhaus Latta, then a natty glass at Cafe Triste.
slots.food: Lunch at Philippe the Original: where the French dip was invented; add the fiery mustard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Tiki-Ti, then a show
slots.text: Sunset Boulevard's beloved little tiki bar, before finding a party or show on the Dice app.
slots.food: Dinner at Quarter Sheets: pies at an Echo Park pizza parlour; save room for dessert.

days.title: East Hollywood, Los Feliz, and Silver Lake

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Walk through Griffith Park
slots.text: Walk through Griffith Park and its observatory.
slots.food: Breakfast at Tacos Villa Corona: a fantastic breakfast burrito from a takeout window.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tom's One Hour Photo
slots.text: Book ahead for a '90s-esque portrait taken by the one and only Tom: the perfect souvenir.
slots.food: Lunch at The Formosa Cafe: a refreshed Hollywood-worthy diner; ask for the converted train car.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Karaoke at Pharaoh
slots.text: Don't leave K-town now: lean in with your own karaoke room.
slots.food: Dinner at Dan Sung Sa: delightfully chaotic Koreatown, soju as quick as the kimchi pancakes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Surf Venice Beach
slots.text: Get past the boardwalk for a surf lesson or a bike ride along the path, then the Santa Monica Pier Ferris wheel.
slots.food: Breakfast at Gjusta: a smoked fish plate with coffee on the sunny patio.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Getty Villa
slots.text: Drive up the coast to this outpost of the Getty, where the Pacific views are showstopping and the villa is pure California decadence.
slots.food: Lunch at La Isla Bonita: fresh ceviche and seafood tostadas served streetside.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Hollywood Forever movie
slots.text: Check the calendar, and if luck has it, pop into the iconic cemetery for a late-night screening.
slots.food: Dinner at Jar: lychee martini, wedge salad and steak in golden-era Hollywood style.

days.title: Grand Canal and the great collections

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
slots.text: An ornate guild headquarters whose ceilings and walls are covered by some of Tintoretto's best works.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ca' Rezzonico
slots.text: An 18th-century palazzo on the Grand Canal, built when a noble family hired the best architects of the day.
slots.food: Lunch at Al Bottegon: a classic bacaro that feels unchanged since the 1950s.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Drinks at Bar Longhi
slots.text: The iconic bar at the Gritti Palace, steeped in literary history and more classic with age.
slots.food: Dinner at Al Timon Bragozzo: lavish cicchetti and strong spritzes, best by the canal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo Correr
slots.text: One of the best places for a crash course in Venetian history, from the city's founding onwards.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
slots.text: A squat palazzo on the Grand Canal, once the home of the eccentric collector who shaped many artists' careers.
slots.food: Lunch at Taverna al Remer: a courtyard tavern with a pier over the canal.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Teatro La Fenice
slots.text: A landmark opera house whose name means The Phoenix, a nod to how it has risen from the ashes three times.
slots.food: Dinner at Wine Bar 5000: exposed brick on a quiet canal, beyond the tourist crowds.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Basilica di Torcello
slots.text: A small 7th-century church with an off-kilter bell tower, plain outside and a Byzantine jewel box within.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museo del Vetro
slots.text: A Gothic palazzo dedicated to Venetian glassblowing, with a collection arranged chronologically.
slots.food: Lunch at Il Santo Bevitore: an old Cannaregio haunt full of devoted regulars.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A glass at Vino Vero
slots.text: A beloved bacaro on a placid Cannaregio canal, with a sign reading No spritz; we love wine!

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
slots.text: The Cathedral Works Museum is one of Florence's finest, in an airy, beautifully lit contemporary space.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museo San Marco
slots.text: Fra Angelico's ethereal, spiritual paintings, in a Dominican convent built between 1437 and 1443.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Aperitivo and craft cocktails
slots.text: A craft cocktail and aperitivo tour that starts in Piazza della Repubblica or on Via dei Tornabuoni.
slots.food: Dinner at Regina Bistecca: steak in a space that was once a 140-year-old antiquarian bookshop.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Vasari Corridor
slots.text: After an eight-year closure, the Vasari Corridor opened to the general public for the first time in December 2024.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Oltrarno: history and artisans
slots.text: A small-group, private walking tour that kicks off in the historic Piazza Santo Spirito.
slots.food: Lunch at Oltrarno Osteria: the younger sister of the popular Osteria dell'Enoteca.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: An evening at the opera
slots.text: Florence's opera house, in a striking contemporary building near the Cascine Park, open since 2011.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo Galileo
slots.text: A Galileo and science tour, from the museum's instruments to the story of Florence's scientific history.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gucci Garden
slots.venue: Gucci Garden (Gucci Museum) & Piazza della Signoria fashion houses
slots.text: Opened in 2011 on the fashion house's 90th anniversary, charting its evolution from the very start.
slots.food: Lunch at Gucci Osteria: a Michelin-starred restaurant in forest green velvet and pea green boiserie.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails at Locale
slots.text: Renaissance pillars, vaulted ceilings and vertical gardens: both a cocktail bar and a fine-dining restaurant.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Rijksmuseum
slots.text: The biggest of Amsterdam's big three museums, alongside the Van Gogh and the Stedelijk, and the largest art museum.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Van Gogh Museum
slots.text: Nowhere else in the world will you find more of the tortured artist's paintings and drawings.
slots.food: Lunch at Rijks: a refined menu in a world-renowned museum setting.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A walk in Vondelpark
slots.text: Amsterdam's version of Central Park, spanning about 120 acres just outside the Canal Ring.
slots.food: Dinner at De Kas: a sunlit, extraordinary setting and vegetable-centric food.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Anne Frank House
slots.text: A 17th-century canal house where entry is by online reservation, so book ahead.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A private canal cruise
slots.text: Slick VIP canal cruises aboard a historic saloon boat, the 1932 teak beauty Welmoed.
slots.food: Lunch at Stubbe's Haring: a timeworn, flag-festooned fish kiosk on the Singel.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A pint at Café de Sluyswacht
slots.text: A lopsided pub whose charm is embracing its quirks, from the stone floors to the staircase.
slots.food: Dinner at Café Schiller: old-fashioned, turn-of-the-century France with French classics.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The ferry to Noord
slots.text: The free ferries shuttle pedestrians and cyclists across the IJ, and are part of how the city gets around.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: STRAAT Museum
slots.text: Amsterdam's second museum devoted to street art, in a colossal warehouse in the former shipbuilding yard.
slots.food: Lunch at Rijsel: classic Flemish dishes in an old-meets-new setting.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A'DAM Toren
slots.text: The blocky A'DAM Tower, directly across from Centraal Station on the other side of the IJ.
slots.food: Dinner at Le Restaurant: a homey, convivial room with next-gen French flavours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: National Gallery of Ireland
slots.text: Re-emerged after a large-scale refurbishment as an impressive gallery that holds its own on the world stage.
slots.food: Breakfast at Kaph: well-prepared espresso in a chill, artsy, cozy space.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Little Museum of Dublin
slots.text: As quirky and eccentric as the city itself, in a gorgeous Georgian townhouse.
slots.food: Lunch at The Woolen Mills Eating House: relaxed charm and river views; come hungry.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Irish Dance Party
slots.text: An interactive show, really a giant party, that will have you on your feet.
slots.food: Dinner at No. 27 Bar & Lounge: seafood in grand rooms, always packed.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Glasnevin Cemetery
slots.text: Famous activists, politicians, artists and writers shaped the city, and many of them are remembered here.
slots.food: Breakfast at Two Pups Coffee: avo toast with peanut butter in a cozy, eclectic space.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Guinness Storehouse
slots.text: The headquarters of Ireland's most famous beer adds culture and history to your vacation drinking.
slots.food: Lunch at The Exchequer: elevated comfort food in a modern pub.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Loose Canon Cheese & Wine
slots.text: A cheese and wine bar worth going back to for the wine and the grilled cheese sandwiches.
slots.food: Dinner at Lemon & Duke: a contemporary neighbourhood bar with on-point drinks.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A dip at Forty Foot
slots.text: Embrace the chill of the Irish Sea at this public swimming spot on the southern tip of Dublin Bay.
slots.food: Breakfast at Brother Hubbard North: daily brunch, relaxed and homey, with flavour-packed mocktails.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Irish Whiskey Museum
slots.text: Exclusively for tourists, and that's okay: it's all part of the experience.
slots.food: Lunch at Meet Me In the Morning: espresso, desserts and brunch bowls in a calm space.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The George
slots.text: A bilevel pub and dance club, lined with portraits of queer icons: a gay haven.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Edinburgh Castle
slots.text: One of the most famous castles in the world, towering above Scotland's capital: probably the most Edinburgh site in Edinburgh.
slots.food: Breakfast at Artisan Roast: standards done right, with scrumptious baked goods.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mary King's Close
slots.text: An Edinburgh alleyway that forms part of the city's famed underground city.
slots.food: Lunch at Civerinos Slice: all the atmosphere you want in a slice joint.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Smith & Gertrude
slots.text: Vinyl records play, servers swoosh over a reclaimed gym floor, and cheese whizzes out on little plates.
slots.food: Dinner at Harajuku Kitchen: Edinburgh's best Japanese restaurant, with quick but relaxing sushi.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gallery of Modern Art
slots.text: Two institutions in one, Modern One and Modern Two, devoted to modern and contemporary art.
slots.food: Breakfast at Söderberg Bakery: eclectic, thoroughly Scandi pastries.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: National Portrait Gallery
slots.text: A gallery rammed with pictures of people you don't know, and far from dull.
slots.food: Lunch at Café Portrait: a continuation of your museum experience, with nibbles and noshes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Stills Gallery
slots.text: A photography gallery with changing exhibitions that often include video or performance.
slots.food: Dinner at Norah: it embodies the shifting culinary landscape in Edinburgh's northeast corner.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Palace of Holyroodhouse
slots.text: The monarch's official Scottish residence, at the foot of the Royal Mile.
slots.food: Breakfast at Twelve Triangles: come for the baked goods in a Willy Wonka-esque wonderland of bread.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Midhope Castle
slots.text: The filming location for Lallybroch, Jamie Fraser's home in the hugely popular Outlander show.
slots.food: Lunch at Archipelago Bakery: a brilliant local bakery serving fresh, organic, wholesome food.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Royal Scottish Academy
slots.text: The Royal Scottish Academy of Art and Architecture, right next to the Scottish National Gallery.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sydney Opera House
slots.text: With its sweeping sails, the symbol of the city, front and center on Sydney Harbour at Bennelong Point.
slots.food: Breakfast at Celsius Coffee Co.: heavenly harbour views and all-day breakfast on a wharf.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sydney Modern
slots.text: The Art Gallery of New South Wales, 150 years after opening, with a major redevelopment and expansion.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Golden Age Cinema and Bar
slots.text: A retro-chic, glamorous, intimate cinema with a handy watering hole attached.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bondi Beach
slots.text: A sweeping, kilometre-long curve of golden sand between two headlands, lashed by surf waves.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Brett Whiteley Studio
slots.text: The home and studio of the late Brett Whiteley, one of Australia's most talented contemporary artists.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cocktails at The Newport
slots.text: An iconic coastal gastropub with a stylish waterfront terrace, cocktails, bubbles and rosé.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Surry Hills
slots.text: Tree-fringed Victorian terrace houses, sociable bars and cafés, and stylish independent shops.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rising Sun Workshop
slots.text: A motorcycle workshop meets cafe, with local brews and Asian savouries for bike fans and foodies.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at Circa 1876
slots.text: Romantic special-occasion dining in a heritage, chandelier-hung cottage, with classy wines.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gastown
slots.text: The quaint neighbourhood between downtown and the cruise ship docks, with cobbled streets.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
slots.venue: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
slots.text: An urban oasis: step out of the downtown bustle and into a classical Chinese garden.
slots.food: Lunch at Anh and Chi: easy, breezy Vietnamese, with the smell of rice noodles and star anise.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bar Gobo
slots.text: Chinatown's endearing 25-seater, the more casual little sister to one-Michelin-starred Burdock & Co.
slots.food: Dinner at Chez Céline: a French restaurant that leans French Canadian.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Stanley Park
slots.text: Regularly heralded as one of the best parks in the world, covering 988 acres.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Granville Island
slots.text: In the 1970s, a polluted waterfront industrial site got a massive makeover.
slots.food: Lunch at Bravo: ocean views and some of the best seafood, at a neighbourhood spot.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bard on the Beach
slots.text: Tents right on the water: one of Vancouver's most unique cultural venues, though seasonal.
slots.food: Dinner at Elisa: Vancouver's swanky steak house.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Grouse Mountain
slots.text: One of the best things about the city is its proximity to nature, and this is where you find it.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Commercial Drive
slots.text: The Drive, as locals call it, is one of Vancouver's most diverse strips and a vibrant cultural hub.
slots.food: Lunch at Elio Volpe: an osteria with a stone hearth oven and the smell of pizza.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Pourhouse
slots.text: A long-time Gastown staple, forever classy, in a building that dates back to 1910.
slots.food: Dinner at Folke: understated elegance at a vegan Kitsilano restaurant.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Art Gallery of Ontario
slots.text: A collection that runs from European masters and Central African artists to emerging Indigenous Canadian artists.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Harbourfront Centre
slots.text: Born of a 1972 federal revitalisation project to boost the waterfront, with the Powerplant gallery.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Library Bar
slots.text: A classic cocktail lounge with an elegant, hushed energy and marble tables.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bata Shoe Museum
slots.text: An award-winning, five-story building by architect Raymond Moriyama is a stylish backdrop for the collection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gardiner Museum
slots.text: One of those museums that leave an impression long after you've left.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bar Pompette
slots.text: At the height of the evening it's alive with a buzzing atmosphere. No reservations, so plan to wait.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Casa Loma
slots.text: The castle of early 20th-century military and business legend Sir Henry Pellatt.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Evergreen Brickworks
slots.text: A 19th-century factory turned into one of Toronto's most charming playgrounds for grown-ups and kids alike.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bar Banane
slots.text: It can be whatever you want: a before-dinner drink, a romantic nightcap, or the main event.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bellagio Conservatory
slots.text: An airy central conservatory that opens up right as you enter Bellagio.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tao Beach Club
slots.text: A Las Vegas day club, so expect a world-class pool party.
slots.food: Lunch at Carbone Riviera: a lakeside dining patio where a yacht drops off sightseeing passengers.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Skyfall Lounge
slots.text: On the 64th floor of the W Las Vegas, formerly the Delano.
slots.food: Dinner at Cote Vegas: Korean barbecue turned into dramatic dinner theater at The Venetian.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Mob Museum
slots.text: Officially the National Museum of Organized Crime and Law Enforcement, in Downtown Las Vegas.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Downtown Arts District
slots.text: For years a motley collection of antiques stores, this part of Downtown has found a new identity.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Rosina
slots.text: Walking in from the casino floor is one of those small Vegas miracles.
slots.food: Dinner at Don's Prime: a deliberate throwback to when a steakhouse dinner was an occasion.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Seven Magic Mountains
slots.text: A large-scale public art work that anyone arriving or leaving Las Vegas via I-15 can see.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Chinatown
slots.text: The three-mile stretch of Spring Mountain Road that runs west toward Mount Charleston from the Strip.
slots.food: Lunch at Gymkhana: a transformed room off the Aria lobby.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: AREA15
slots.text: A massive entertainment zone just across I-15 from the Las Vegas Strip.
slots.food: Dinner at Maroon by Kwame Onwuachi: someone will welcome you home.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: SFMOMA
slots.venue: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
slots.text: Stands out among the city's elite museums for its innovative, exciting exhibits.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Asian Art Museum
slots.text: A massive collection, all housed in a gorgeous Beaux Arts building.
slots.food: Lunch at Minnie Bell's Soul Movement: a vibrant mural of Fillmore Street, circa 1962.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Club Fugazi
slots.text: A historic theater tucked into North Beach, once home to the long-running Beach Blanket Babylon.
slots.food: Dinner at Maria Isabel: a custom oak door opening into a richly layered dining room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ferry to Sausalito
slots.text: San Francisco's largest ferry company takes passengers to big-name destinations around the bay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Angel Island
slots.text: Hop on the Golden Gate Ferry from the Ferry Building, or the Angel Island Tiburon Ferry from Tiburon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Magic Theater
slots.text: Step downstairs near Union Square into the Oasis Lounge, a former speakeasy.
slots.food: Dinner at Four Kings: a bit of a Hong Kong fever dream, a bit of an apartment dinner party.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Haight-Ashbury
slots.text: Named for the intersection of two streets, but the name is much bigger than that.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sunset Dunes Park
slots.text: Public art installations dot the route, and sandy access points lead directly onto the beach.
slots.food: Lunch at Mijoté: warm, natural tones and a long, gleaming wood bar.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: ABV
slots.text: A bar that feels like slipping into a well-worn leather jacket.
slots.food: Dinner at Azalina's: in the Tenderloin, channelling the night street food stalls of Penang.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Grand Palace
slots.venue: The Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha)
slots.text: A sprawling complex, though the Thai royal family moved out by 1925.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Wat Pho
slots.venue: Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha)
slots.text: The main draw is the country's largest reclining Buddha, a 150-foot-long sculpture.
slots.food: Lunch at Nai Ek Roll Noodles: stall after stall of wok-fried noodles, dumplings and char-grilled seafood.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Wat Arun
slots.text: One of the most iconic of Thailand's more than 40,000 temples, with a 269-foot-tall prang.
slots.food: Dinner at Charmgang: the name Bangkokians repeat when taking out-of-town friends for a meal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Jim Thompson House
slots.text: The home of American Jim Thompson, an officer at the OSS stationed in Thailand during World War II.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Blue Elephant Cooking School
slots.text: Bringing home a taste of Thai food is high on most travellers' lists, so learn how in a class.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Manohra Dinner River Cruise
slots.text: An antique wooden rice barge bobs on the Chao Phraya River to a soundtrack of Thai string instruments.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Talat Noi Street Art
slots.text: A small alley with murals in one of Bangkok's trendiest neighbourhoods.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Benchakitti Park
slots.text: Around since 1994, with a brand-new 120-acre expansion that makes it a beautiful green space.
slots.food: Lunch at Wana Yook: from Thai-Indian chef Chalee Kader, behind some of Bangkok's most emblematic restaurants.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Soi Nana
slots.text: Chinatown's Soi Nana is Bangkok's best bar-hopping street, not to be confused with the seedy one on Sukhumvit Road.
slots.food: Dinner at Côte by Mauro Colagreco: a white-tablecloth dining room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Pura Ulun Danu Bratan
slots.text: Known as Bali's floating temple, a 17th-century Hindu-Buddhist temple set against a backdrop of mountains and water.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jatiluwih Rice Terraces
slots.venue: Jatiluwih rice terraces & the Subak system
slots.text: Peaceful and tranquil, with a vast, emerald-green landscape that is almost mesmerizing.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Syrco BASÈ
slots.text: A chef who spent more than a decade cooking in the Netherlands, now cooking in Ubud.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sekumpul Waterfall
slots.text: In North Bali's sedate countryside, considered by many to be the island's finest waterfall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tirta Gangga
slots.text: A former palace turned lavish water gardens that looks like it has existed for centuries.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Pica South American Kitchen
slots.text: Centrally located on Ubud's bustling Jalan Dewi Sita strip, with a small and intimate feel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Suluban Beach
slots.text: Hidden between dramatic limestone cliffs, a west-facing beach in Uluwatu that is a haven for surfers and photographers.
slots.food: Breakfast at Sisterfields: an all-day Australian breakfast cafe.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Potato Head Beach Club
slots.text: Part beach club, part hotel and part cultural village: a hub for food, drink and design.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ghost Kitchen & Record Bar
slots.text: A buzzy Canggu spot with several ways to spend the night, depending on the night you want.
slots.food: Dinner at Sangsaka: hidden down a nondescript road in Seminyak.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia
slots.text: Tucked into a corner of Federation Square, with more than 20 individual galleries across three levels.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Australian Centre for the Moving Image
slots.text: A museum dedicated to everything in Australia related to the screen: film, television and more.
slots.food: Lunch at Supernormal: one of the best spots for pan-Asian cooking in Melbourne.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Moon Dog Craft Brewery
slots.text: Brewers who aren't known for playing it safe, in an old brick warehouse.
slots.food: Dinner at Longsong: upscale BBQ with Asian accents in a loose, lively room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Melbourne Museum
slots.text: Get ready to learn everything there is to learn about Melbourne, in a museum that opened in 2001.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Immigration Museum
slots.text: Tells the story of Australia, which was inhabited by First Nations people long before the last two centuries.
slots.food: Lunch at Etta: the neighbourhood restaurant of your dreams.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: St. Kilda Beach
slots.text: If you visit Melbourne and don't step foot on the St. Kilda sand, were you even there?
slots.food: Dinner at Smith & Daughters: a celebratory fine-dining mainstay with buzzy cocktails.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: NGV International
slots.text: When the National Gallery of Victoria's collection became too vast, it needed a second home.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Lyon Housemuseum
slots.text: The super-stylish home of architect Corbett Lyon and family, who live among a vast art collection.
slots.food: Lunch at Osteria Ilaria: fortifying food in a remarkably pleasant European atmosphere.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at Ides
slots.text: Mystery and daring offset by deliciousness, in an enigmatic room with an intriguing crowd.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: St. Andrew's Cathedral
slots.text: A giant, wedding-cake-like monument in the middle of the Civic District: you can't miss it.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Marina Bay Sands
slots.text: A massive Moshe Safdie-designed mall, casino, convention center and hotel, perhaps Singapore's most iconic building.
slots.food: Lunch at Summer Palace: a fine-dining Cantonese institution.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Clarke Quay
slots.text: A beautiful riverside quay that is home to a clutch of historic warehouses.
slots.food: Dinner at Restaurant Fiz: on Tanjong Pagar Road, echoing the area's heritage.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sri Mariamman Temple
slots.text: The oldest Hindu temple in Singapore, and one of the most recognizable.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Thian Hock Keng
slots.text: Singapore's oldest Hokkien temple, with elaborate architecture.
slots.food: Lunch at Seroja: soulful food in an unexpectedly shiny mixed-use development.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sago House
slots.text: Ranked among Asia's top bars on the World's Best list, though don't expect anything fancy.
slots.food: Dinner at Somma, in New Bahru: unwrapped with a flourish, like a dish from under a cloche.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Singapore Cable Car
slots.venue: Singapore Cable Car (Mount Faber to Sentosa)
slots.text: Cable cars run from Mount Faber to Sentosa, with a stop at HarbourFront in between.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sentosa
slots.text: A 1,236-acre island resort off the southern coast, home to major tourist attractions.
slots.food: Lunch at GUUM Contemporary Grill: Korean barbecue, but not the casual greasy-floor joint.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Fura
slots.text: Singapore's most progressive and sustainability-focused bar, with its menus on display outside.
slots.food: Dinner at Na Oh: reached through Hyundai's innovation center, an all-white minimalist space.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tai Kwun
slots.venue: Tai Kwun: Centre for Heritage & Arts
slots.text: Hong Kong never wastes a square foot, and this heritage-and-arts compound is a rare open space in a dense city.
slots.food: Breakfast at Luk Yu Tea House: dating back to 1933, one of Central's oldest restaurants.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Blue House
slots.text: In hyper-dense Hong Kong, a rare pre-World War II building that hasn't been razed or modernized.
slots.food: Lunch at Chau Kee, in the charming Sai Ying Pun neighbourhood.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Tin Lung Heen
slots.text: Hovering above the city on the 102nd floor of The Ritz-Carlton.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Chi Lin Nunnery
slots.venue: Chi Lin Nunnery & Nan Lian Garden
slots.text: Hong Kong may be one of the fastest-paced cities in the world, but it has its quiet corners too.
slots.food: Breakfast at Let's Yum Cha: dim sum, with photos of steaming baskets on the wall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: West Kowloon Cultural District
slots.text: What was once part of Victoria Harbour is now Hong Kong's dedicated hub for arts and culture.
slots.food: Lunch at Dragon Noodles Academy: iconic black-and-gold calligraphy on the shop sign.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Spring Moon
slots.text: The Cantonese restaurant at the legendary Peninsula Hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: DolphinWatch Tour
slots.text: A half-day tour to see one of Hong Kong's most endangered residents, the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Lamma Island
slots.text: Just 20 to 30 minutes from Hong Kong Island by ferry.
slots.food: Lunch at Kin's Kitchen: a fifth-floor restaurant where the lift opens straight onto the dining room.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Maxim's Palace
slots.text: On the second floor of City Hall in Central, channelling old-school Cantonese opulence.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Abu Dhabi Heritage Village
slots.text: Run by the Emirates Heritage Club, a reconstructed traditional village.
slots.food: Breakfast at Tawa Bakery: a seaside cuppa and a fully gluten-free menu.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Zayed Heritage Center
slots.text: A small, humble museum, the perfect place for history buffs.
slots.food: Lunch at Alba Terrace: a refined Mediterranean brunch with a spritz cart.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Emirates Palace Spa
slots.text: The perfect example of Middle Eastern tranquility, luxurious and palatial.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: N2N Gallery
slots.text: A tiny but notable gallery showing sculpture, graphic art and paintings by mostly European artists.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Emirates National Auto Museum
slots.text: Beyond the city center, on the edge of the desert, a museum with an impressive collection.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Remede Spa
slots.text: Like its setting, The St Regis Abu Dhabi, all about exceeding expectations.
slots.food: Dinner at The Foundry: a sultry steakhouse for people who are here for the meat.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Etihad Modern Art Gallery
slots.text: A snazzy modern art gallery showing some of the best contemporary artworks.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: CHI, the Spa at Shangri-La
slots.text: True to Shangri-La's Hong Kong roots, the atmosphere feels distinctly Asia-inspired.
slots.food: Lunch at Oléa: a late-morning feast in a grand ballroom.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sanderson's
slots.text: Its green canopy is what first catches the eye.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Castle of Good Hope
slots.text: A sprawling 17th-century site near the shoreline of Table Bay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: District Six Museum
slots.text: Tells the story of District Six, a vibrant, mixed-race community.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Evita Se Perron
slots.text: A quirky cabaret hall whose evenings are hard to sum up in a line.
slots.food: Dinner at Nikkei: from Sydney hospitality maestros Swillhouse.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Robben Island Museum
slots.text: The island, about five miles off the coast of Cape Town, is now a museum.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Camps Bay Beach
slots.text: Cape Town's party beach: a long stretch of white sand bordered by a promenade.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at Amura
slots.text: At the storied Mount Nelson, A Belmond Hotel, with more to it than the setting.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Iziko South African Museum
slots.text: Home to thousands of interesting artifacts.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Norval Foundation
slots.text: The most buzzed-about art center to open in Cape Town in years.
slots.food: Lunch at The Skotnes Restaurant: part of the ultra-contemporary arts centre.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at Emazulwini
slots.text: Contemporary Zulu and Nguni cuisine, rarely sampled by visitors, in a swank setting.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: BA Free Tour
slots.text: Both homespun and pro, led by the fun, friendly Sol.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Shop Hop Buenos Aires
slots.text: A guided shopping tour that starts with an online style assessment before you even meet up.
slots.food: Lunch at Picarón: a colourful facade with a bear on a velocipede as its logo.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: La Ventana
slots.text: A tango show in a historic conventillo in San Telmo, with exposed brick walls.
slots.food: Dinner at Alcanfor: a simple Villa Crespo bistro with a small, open kitchen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo de Arte Tigre
slots.text: Housed in one of Tigre's most stunning Belle Epoque palaces.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museo del Mate
slots.text: A relatively intimate museum overlooking Tigre's main waterway.
slots.food: Lunch at Ness: a former warehouse on a quiet corner of a leafy suburb, 40 minutes from downtown.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: El Querandí
slots.text: A restored 1920s mansion atmosphere, with high ceilings and period details.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Art Insider Tour
slots.text: A private, extremely organised tour that begins with a questionnaire about your art tastes.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Parrilla Tour
slots.text: A group walking tour for around 12 diners that leaves you stuffed and ready for a siesta.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at Han
slots.text: From the street you see only a massive door and the word Han; you ring the doorbell.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
slots.text: If you only have time for one museum, make it this one, housed in a neoclassical-style mansion.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Historic Triangle
slots.text: A tangle of streets, stoas and pedestrian alleys wedged between Syntagma, Omonia and Monastiraki squares, for shopping and bar-hopping.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cinema Paradiso
slots.text: Athens is a city of cinephiles: Athenians prefer arthouse flicks in retro picture houses to soulless multiplexes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kerameikos
slots.text: The most moving, and often overlooked, of the archaeological sites around the Acropolis: the ancient cemetery.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museum of Contemporary Art (EMST)
slots.text: After several false starts, it has hit its stride since Katerina Gregos became artistic director.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Picnic with the ancients
slots.text: The best vantage point of the Parthenon without the crowds: follow the pedestrian boulevard circling the Acropolis.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Zoodochos Pigi Street
slots.text: A scruffy, narrow street running the length of Exarchia, epitomizing the creative and often contradictory currents of the neighbourhood.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Hit the beach
slots.text: The Athens Riviera stretches 35 miles from Paleo Faliro to the temple of Poseidon at Cape Sounion.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hit the bottle
slots.text: Greek wine is long past cheap retsina in a tin jug, and now wins global accolades.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Philosopher's Path
slots.text: Follow in the footsteps of philosopher Kitaro Nishida along a quiet stone walk through the scenic Higashiyama district.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gion
slots.text: Most visitors come to Kyoto's most famous district hoping to spot geisha, often crowding the main roads with cameras.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nokishita 77
slots.text: Near Pontocho's lantern-lit lanes, a narrow, crepuscular hideaway where a former chef serves what he calls liquid cuisine.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Saihō-ji Temple
slots.text: Known as Kokedera, or Moss Temple, this UNESCO World Heritage site is carpeted in moss, and stands apart in a city famous for gardens.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Blue Bottle Studio
slots.text: For those who believe coffee is as much ritual as refreshment. Open only in spring and autumn.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Shakusui-en Garden
slots.text: Hidden within the Four Seasons Kyoto, an 800-year-old garden: an oasis combining history and nature.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kamigamo Jinja Shrine
slots.text: Far from the tourist throngs in the city's north, a UNESCO World Heritage site that feels like a hidden secret.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Cocoo Urushi Lacquerware Workshop
slots.text: On the northern edge of the Nishijin weaving district, an intimate introduction to urushi, Japan's centuries-old lacquer tradition.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The House of Ki No Bi
slots.venue: The House of Ki No Bi
slots.text: In a century-old machiya once home to a wood merchant, gin geekery meets Kyoto craftsmanship.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Lay siege to the castle
slots.text: A must on a first visit: a sprawling UNESCO World Heritage site mixing Gothic, baroque and Renaissance architecture.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tram 42
slots.text: A hop-on-hop-off service on vintage trams that scoots around some of the city's favourite streets and landmarks.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bar-hopping on the embankment
slots.text: The Vltava quayside, once half-forgotten and used for storage and parking, is now a stretch of bars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kunsthalle Praha
slots.text: Opened in 2022 in a former electric station in the centre of the city, for modern art beyond the Mucha poster.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Retro Museum
slots.text: On the top floor of the brutalist Kotva department store: yellow-and-orange wallpaper, Formica and plasticware.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Prague's beer culture
slots.text: Czechia has a deserved reputation for pilsner, which flows from pedal-powered beer buses to spas with tubs of the stuff.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Climb a tower
slots.text: Prague's architects built several towers for vantage points, and around 120 of them make a quick workout.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Manifesto Market
slots.text: In the off-the-radar Andel district, for a snapshot of the city's contemporary street food culture.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Praha 7
slots.text: A former industrial quarter in a bend of the river, reborn with street-food stalls, farmers' markets and galleries.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Walk the line
slots.text: One of the world's most giddying hikes runs along the rim of the flooded volcano from Fira to Oia: three hours of mind-blowing vistas.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Go off-piste in Oia
slots.text: Undeniably the most spectacular village on the island, but a hot mess of coach parties and selfie sticks at peak times.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Seek out another sunset
slots.text: Each evening crowds flock to Oia's high-flung castle to clap the sun's descent over the caldera's black rim.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Akrotiri
slots.venue: Akrotiri archaeological site, the Minoan Pompeii
slots.text: One of the most powerful settlements in the Aegean before a volcanic eruption destroyed it around 3,600 years ago.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The inland villages
slots.text: While everyone oohs over the cliffside views, life goes quietly on in Santorini's inland villages.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Taste the finest wines
slots.text: Vineyards are dotted around the island, the grapes pinned close to the porous earth by wreaths of vine branches.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kayak around the caldera
slots.text: For a more adventurous take on the sunset cruise, paddle your own kayak past the famous Red and White beaches.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Swim in search of Atlantis
slots.text: Santorini is the likely inspiration for Plato's lost kingdom of Atlantis, so where better to go scuba diving?

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Charter your own catamaran
slots.text: Cheesy might be the word that springs to mind, but chartering your own is a different thing from the hordes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Hagia Sophia
slots.text: From outside, undeniably majestic: a seemingly floating central dome flanked by four spear-like minarets.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Topkapi Palace
slots.text: Perched above the Bosphorus in the Fatih district, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Basilica Cistern
slots.text: A miniature doorway beside the Hagia Sophia leads down a narrow flight of stone steps to the cistern.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Grand Bazaar
slots.text: Founded in 1461 and beautifully restored: one of the world's oldest and largest indoor markets, with more than 60 covered streets.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bosphorus river cruise
slots.text: The Bosphorus Strait connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, dividing Istanbul's east and west.
slots.food: Lunch at Hanimeli Vegan: an unassuming hole-in-the-wall café in Cihangir; point and order.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Galata Tower
slots.text: One of Istanbul's most instantly recognizable landmarks, built in 1348 and on the UNESCO list since 2013.
slots.food: Dinner at Karaköy Lokantası: attentive service, an impressive wine list and a jovial atmosphere.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Zeyrek Çinili Hammam
slots.text: Reopened in September 2023 after a 13-year restoration: a 16th-century treasure in the UNESCO-listed Zeyrek neighbourhood.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Museum of Innocence
slots.text: Novelist Orhan Pamuk's museum, spread over five floors of a 19th-century crimson wooden house in Çukurcuma.
slots.food: Lunch at Tatbak: spicy minced-meat lahmacun, worth the 40-minute walk from Çukurcuma.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Istanbul Modern
slots.text: Among the first to lead the contemporary art wave when it opened in 2004, recently relocated.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Como's historic center
slots.text: Clinging to the lake's southwestern pocket, an ideal jumping-off point whose medieval wall still stands.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Silk Museum
slots.text: Como became Italy's silk capital in the 19th century, and remains at the top of its game as designers worldwide use its silk.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Casabianca
slots.text: A new venue in Como showcasing the De Santis family's extensive contemporary art collection.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Villa del Balbianello
slots.text: On a lakeside peninsula in Tremezzina, an elaborate 18th-century complex that James Bond and Star Wars fans will recognise.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Isola Comacina
slots.text: The lake's only island, beside Tremezzina's shoreline, inhabited as far back as the Roman era, with the ruins to prove it.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A boat ride on the lake
slots.text: The lake is most evocative from the water, and public ferries let you hop on and off with a day pass.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: I Vetri di Bellagio
slots.text: Bellagio is one of the lake's most trodden towns, and its heirlooms are still well worth finding.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Orrido di Bellano
slots.text: A 15-million-year-old gorge cut into the craggy hillside, known for its roaring 66-foot waterfall and multi-level walkways.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Borgo Corenno Plinio
slots.text: An exquisite medieval hamlet nicknamed the village of 1000 steps, which evokes the transportive powers of time travel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Amalfi Cathedral
slots.text: The thousand-year-old centerpiece of Amalfi's compact historic center, with hidden courtyards and stairways beyond.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museo della Carta
slots.text: A history lesson in the region's papermaking tradition, inside a historic 13th-century paper mill.
slots.food: Afternoon treat at Pasticceria Pansa: the dome-shaped delizia al limone, a lemon cream-filled sponge cake.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Le Sirenuse Mare
slots.text: Arrive by boat and stay until sunset, from the tiered beach club to lunch under the pergolas.
slots.food: The langoustine carpaccio with caviar is a must-order, then gelato or a granita at the Dolce Far Niente Bar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Villa Cimbrone
slots.text: Botanical gardens, rose gardens and a medieval cloister, crowned by the Terrace of Infinity nearly 1,200 feet above the sea.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ceramics in Ravello
slots.text: Browse handcrafted pieces at Pascal Ceramiche D'Arte, or artisan-crafted sandals at Bottega Eva Caruso.
slots.food: Cool off with gelato from Baffone Gelateria Artigianale.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Clubhouse by the Sea
slots.text: Steps lead down to intimate gardens and sunbeds in the rocky shoreline, with views of yachts and slick Riva boats.
slots.food: Freshly baked pizzas and seafood pasta by the water.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Path of the Gods
slots.text: A 4.3-mile former shepherd's trail that ends above Positano; descend 1,700 timeworn stone steps to the town.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Vietri sul Mare
slots.venue: Vietri sul Mare: the Ceramics Town
slots.text: A centuries-old ceramics heritage, with small workshops and family factories still making hand-painted pieces.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Positano
slots.text: At Emporio Sirenuse, Le Sirenuse's flagship store, find caftans and accessories inspired by Amalfi.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Parra's coconut tree road
slots.text: Now Instagram-famous but quiet at daybreak, when the fields are misty.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Fort Aguada
slots.text: A trail winds past trees and stone outcrops to a dramatic headland where the Mandovi River meets the Arabian Sea.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Pablo's, Assagao
slots.text: Local beers and feni, a spirit made from fermented cashew apples or coconut sap: uncomplicated and very Goan.
slots.food: Dinner at Izumi Assagao: the yuzu prawn tempura maki and hamachi truffle ponzu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museum of Christian Art
slots.text: In the 17th-century Convent of Santa Monica in Old Goa, showing the imprint of Indian artisanship on early church objects.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museum of Goa
slots.text: Contemporary art that tells the story of the state's history and culture, with a great souvenir shop.
slots.food: Lunch at Spice Goa in Sangolda: piquant seafood, including a lobster dish.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Anjuna
slots.text: Authentic handmade pasta at Al Pomodoro in Anjuna.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Calangute and Baga beaches
slots.text: Just after sunrise even the busiest beaches, Calangute, Baga and Candolim, are empty until about 7 a.m.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Paper Boat Collective
slots.text: In Sangolda, marine-inspired tableware, home decor and art pieces by Thomas the Potter.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Room One and Drop Dead Sexy
slots.text: An experimental cocktail space and an art-forward bar, both in Assagao.
slots.food: Dinner at Grumps in Sangolda: Sichuan fried chicken and lamb krapow kebabs.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Karura Forest
slots.text: Without a doubt the most scenic route in the city, and the second largest urban forest in the world.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Nairobi Gallery
slots.text: Home to Point Zero, the spot from which all distances in Kenya are measured.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Talisman
slots.text: A Nairobi stalwart where a corner table by the fireplace on a chilly evening is a date-night dream.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Brackenhurst and the tea plantations
slots.text: Coffee from Muna Tree Cafe on the terrace, then a rented bicycle through rolling tea plantations.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Spinners Web and Tribal Gallery
slots.text: Spinners Web has rugs, a café and a used-books library; Tribal Gallery has restored Swahili doors and oversized mirrors.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Fig & Olive, Tigoni
slots.text: Part bodega, part restaurant, with a lawn where no one blinks if you swap your chair for the grass.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Toi Market
slots.text: Sprawling, busy and a little chaotic: an open-air flea-market vibe with thousands of stalls.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: McMillan Memorial Library
slots.text: A perfect little time capsule of Nairobi, architecturally and literally, now being renovated by Book Bunk.
slots.food: Lunch at Tin Roof Café in Karen: the salad bar is iconic.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Geco and Cave-à-Manger
slots.text: Geco is alive with Nairobi's music scene, especially on Wednesdays; Cave-à-Manger has an expansive wine list.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace
slots.text: First established in 1395, burned down in the 16th century, rebuilt, plundered and rebuilt again: still singularly beautiful.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Changdeokgung Palace
slots.text: Look up at the detailed roof of this royal palace.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Insa-dong
slots.text: A picturesque neighbourhood of hanoks, traditional Korean houses, with art museums, galleries, restaurants and cafés.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Leeum Museum of Art
slots.text: An extraordinary permanent collection of Korean ceramics, on a slight hill in an art-rich part of the city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gyeongdong Market
slots.text: An outdoor market where chef Kang Mingoo buys ingredients, with stalls devoted to jang, fermented pastes.
slots.food: Lunch at Hansung Kalguksu: a casual Gangnam spot for knife-cut noodles.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Mingles
slots.text: Kang Mingoo's Michelin-spangled restaurant in Gangnam, mixing tradition with innovative techniques and global influences.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Wear a hanbok
slots.text: Locals and tourists dress in hanboks, partly because shops in the neighbourhood often discount for anyone in a rented one.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Seongsu-dong
slots.text: A trendy, formerly industrial neighbourhood, with a pop-up complex of 200 blue shipping containers and a rice mill turned café.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Frieze House
slots.text: Frieze launched in Seoul in 2022, and its permanent art space, Frieze House, debuted last year.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Little Venice and the windmills
slots.text: Many of the outdoor tables in Little Venice are just inches from the tide, with the windmills above.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Agios Sostis beach
slots.text: A quieter day at a beach away from the beach-club scene.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sea Satin
slots.text: The late-night dining room beneath the windmills, where white napkins circle overhead and people climb onto the tables.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Psarou and Nammos
slots.text: At Nammos, polished excess: sunny days move from beach beds at Psarou into a long fish lunch and dancing.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Scorpios
