slots.text: About 85 metres deep, with churches, dining halls and stables, once home to around 30,000. Only 10% can be visited.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kaymaklı Underground City
slots.text: Eight floors carved underground, with houses linked by hidden passages that protected against enemies.
slots.food: Dried clotted cream with honey, or sherbet, in the town.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ürgüp
slots.text: The most touristic and bustling town in Cappadocia, with elegant restaurants and nightlife. See the Three Beauties fairy chimneys.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ihlara Valley
slots.text: One of Turkey's largest canyons, with a walk past cave churches with wall paintings. A 14-kilometre route reaches Belisırma.
slots.food: Tea in the pergolas over the Melendiz Stream.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Avanos pottery
slots.text: The centre of pottery since the Hittite period. Make your own with an instructor, and visit the 2nd-century Yamanlı Church.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Zelve
slots.text: The densest site of fairy chimneys, in three valleys, which glow crimson in the setting sun.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Charminar
slots.text: Built in 1591, with four soaring minarets and a bazaar at its base. Walk the precinct early to dodge the crowds.
slots.food: Cafe Nimrah, next to the monument, for Irani chai and an Osmania biscuit.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Chowmahalla Palace and Laad Bazaar
slots.text: Where the Nizams were crowned, then Laad Bazaar for lacquered bangles and bridal finery.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hyderabadi biryani
slots.text: Hyderabadi biryani made the top 10 of TasteAtlas's best rice dishes in 2025. Try the kacchi, pakki or sealed dum versions.
slots.food: Paradise, Shah Ghouse and Bawarchi, with mirchi salan or raita.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Salar Jung Museum
slots.text: 46,000 art pieces from Mughal miniatures to European sculpture, and the Veiled Rebecca. Weekday mornings avoid school trips.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Paigah Tombs
slots.text: A late 18th-century necropolis blending eight architectural styles, with over 35 jaali patterns. Closed Fridays.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Falaknuma Palace
slots.venue: Taj Falaknuma Palace: high tea and heritage walk
slots.text: Italian marble staircases and chandeliers; the Adaa restaurant's 101-foot table is said to be the world's longest.
slots.food: Nizami cuisine, including the Jauzi halwa.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Qutb Shahi Tombs
slots.text: The Seven Tombs sit in a 106-acre heritage park with over 70 monuments, ideal at sunrise or golden hour.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Golconda Fort
slots.text: Pair the tombs with the nearby fort for a full-day heritage binge.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bar Kin Rü
slots.text: A craft bar serving Mughal-inspired dishes, with theatrical cocktails on the fifth floor, in India's Top 30 Bars list for 2024.
slots.food: The Jackfruit Haleem.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Galle Fort and the lighthouse
slots.text: A UNESCO site over the Indian Ocean, with ramparts resembling those on Portugal's coast and a lighthouse that has guided sailors ashore.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Maritime and National museums
slots.text: The Maritime Archaeology Museum in the Fort, then the Galle National Museum, in a building from 1656.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Old Dutch Hospital
slots.text: The former Dutch hospital is now a shopping complex of restaurants, boutiques and gem shops.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dutch Reformed Church
slots.text: An elegant church from 1754 in the Fort, with its records of marriages and baptisms. Admire the Dutch houses and the Dutch gate.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Galapatha Temple
slots.text: Not far from the main city, it houses the tooth relic of Arhat Maha Kassapa.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Galleries and antique shops
slots.venue: The Boutique, Gem & Gallery Lanes of the Fort
slots.text: The Fort's houses have been turned into restaurants, art galleries, antique shops and fashionable boutiques.
slots.food: End at a pleasant street-side café.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Midigama
slots.text: A golden beach near Galle with palm trees, turquoise water and the south coast's unique stilt fishermen.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Talalla
slots.text: A tranquil beach with soft golden sand, for swimming or surfing, away from the bustle.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hiriketiya Bay
slots.text: A horseshoe-shaped cove in Dickwella with a tranquil shore, turquoise water and swaying coconut palms.

days.title: Dhoni cruising and an underwater dinner

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dhoni boat cruise
slots.text: A traditional dhoni takes you to a new destination each day, with snorkelling spots, reefs, uninhabited islands and local villages.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Parasailing
slots.text: Led by a speedboat, a parachute lifts you high over the islands and reefs. Available at most major resorts.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: SEA at Anantara Kihavah
slots.text: An underwater restaurant where sharks, turtles and fish pass by as you eat Maldivian cuisine.
slots.food: The fresh Maldivian lobster.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: South Ari Atoll
slots.text: Swim with huge, harmless whale sharks in the South Ari Atoll, near Sun Island and Rangali Island.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Underwater spa at Huvafen Fushi
slots.text: The world's first underwater spa retreat, for adults only, with massages using the island's coconut oil.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Subsix at Niyama
slots.text: The world's first underwater nightclub. The glow party runs on Wednesdays and Saturdays from 9pm.

days.title: Island culture in the Baa Atoll

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Thulhaadhoo
slots.text: A small Baa Atoll island of lacquerware artisans, reached from Malé by speedboat, ferry or hydroplane.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Maalhos
slots.text: A traditional fishing village of about 600 people, one of the oldest islands in the Baa Atoll, for relaxing and snorkelling.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Finolhu
slots.text: An island resort with a beach club, where the 1 Oak Beach Club comes alive at sunset with cocktails and performers.
slots.food: Tuesday's Seafood Extravaganza at the Fish and Crab Shack.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Leh Palace
slots.text: Spend your first days in Leh, resting while you acclimatise. The 17th-century palace shows a Tibetan influence in its architecture.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Shanti Stupa
slots.text: One of Leh's most gorgeous sights, with the outskirts holding Magnetic Hill, Sangam and Gurudwara Pathar Sahib.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Leh Market
slots.venue: Leh café evenings: Gesmo & the Main Bazaar
slots.text: Wander the market on foot after the day, with cafés and bars. Lehchen is one of the city's few bars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Khardung La
slots.venue: Khardung La (Among The World's Highest Passes)
slots.text: The road to Nubra climbs over one of the highest motorable passes, so start early and allow for traffic at the photo stops.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Diskit Monastery
slots.text: In Nubra, the cold desert turns green for a short while. One night is enough for the double-humped Bactrian camels and Diskit Monastery.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Nubra camp
slots.text: Many travellers simply arrive and choose a stay in person, while higher-end luxury camps are worth booking ahead.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Chang La
slots.text: Cross Chang La on the way to Pangong, allowing for the tiring altitude and for stops for tea and photos.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pangong Tso
slots.text: The brackish lake shifts through blue, green and grey depending on the sunlight, and freezes over in winter. Part of it lies in China.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A night by the lake
slots.text: Accommodation here is limited, dry and remote. One night is enough to experience the lake.

days.title: The Taj Mahal and Agra Fort

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Taj Mahal
slots.text: Shah Jahan's marble tomb for Mumtaz Mahal, built from 1632 to 1648, with minarets, lotus motifs and floral patterns. Allow at least half a day.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Agra Fort
slots.text: The seat of the Mughal court for over a century, and a UNESCO site. Exploring it takes more than three hours; pair it with the Taj.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Mehtab Bagh
slots.text: A garden across the Yamuna, behind the Taj, with uninterrupted views of the mausoleum and good sunset light.
slots.food: Dinner at Taj Bano, one of the city's best restaurants.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Fatehpur Sikri
slots.text: Akbar's red sandstone capital, used from 1571 to 1585: the Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal and Diwan-i-Khas. Allow up to five hours.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Salim Chishti's tomb
slots.venue: The Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri
slots.text: The latticework tomb of the Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chishti, inside the Jama Masjid complex.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner in the Old City
slots.text: Back in Agra, inexpensive eating in the Old City.
slots.food: Puris at Chimman Lal Poori, or spiced nihari at Mughal Nihari.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
slots.text: Completed by Jahangir in 1613. Nearby is the tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani, built between 1623 and 1627.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Chini ka Rauza
slots.text: The Prime Minister's tomb by the Yamuna, known for its Indo-Persian style and glazed tile work, near Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sadar Bazaar
slots.text: Leather at Sadar Bazaar, silk at Subhash Bazar, and handicrafts and jewellery at Kinari Bazar.
slots.food: Petha, the candied ash gourd, and dalmoth, a savoury snack.

days.title: The Golden Temple and Jallianwala Bagh

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Golden Temple
slots.text: Best at the Amrit Vela, between 4 and 6am, or when the temple lights shimmer on the water in the late evening.
slots.food: Join the community meal in the langar hall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jallianwala Bagh
slots.text: A short walk from the temple: the narrow lane, the Martyrs' Well and the bullet-marked walls. It opens at 6:30am.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Town Hall
slots.text: A red 1860s building near the Golden Temple, now cafés, restaurants and street food stalls, lit up at night.
slots.food: Dinner at Rang Punjab, a vegetarian dhaba inside.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Partition Museum
slots.text: Inside Town Hall, with testimonies, letters and old trunks. Open 10am to 5pm; plan at least two hours.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gobindgarh Fort
slots.text: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's former stronghold, with a coin museum, a 7D film and a light-and-sound show at night.
slots.food: A lane of stalls with kulchas, lassi and jalebis.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Wagah Border
slots.text: About 30 km from Amritsar, where the Indian and Pakistani guards put on a ceremony of energy and precision.

days.title: The old city and its food

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The walled city
slots.text: Walk the narrow lanes before 8am, with Mughal, Sikh and colonial buildings and horse carriages.
slots.food: Kulcha at Pehalwan Kulcha, open since 1953, then lassi.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gurudwara Baba Atal Sahib
slots.text: Climb to the terrace for a view of the Golden Temple and the city. The stairs open 7 to 10am and 3 to 6pm.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Crystal
slots.text: A fine-dining restaurant on Queens Road since 1935, with Victorian ceiling and vintage European charm.
slots.food: Chinese and Indian dishes, and the softy ice cream outside.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Cellular Jail
slots.text: The chilling British-built 1906 national memorial, where political prisoners were once held.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ross Island
slots.venue: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep)
slots.text: The jungle-wreathed Victorian ruins of the colonial-era administrative headquarters, used until 1941.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The ferry to Havelock
slots.text: Private ferries link Port Blair and Havelock. They usually open for booking, including online, at least a month ahead.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sunrise at Kalapathar
slots.text: Catch the sunrise at Kalapathar on Havelock, the most developed of the islands, with silky beaches backed by rainforest.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Diving or snorkelling
slots.text: The diving and snorkelling rival the best in South Asia, to spot wrecks, sharks, rays and turtles.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Radhanagar Beach
slots.text: One of Asia's most spectacular beaches, for a stroll before dinner.
slots.food: Home-cooked dinners at Full Moon Café or Anju-Coco Resto.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Elephant Beach
slots.text: Hike into the lushly forested interior to Elephant Beach, or join a kayaking expedition through the mangroves.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Neil Island
slots.text: A flat, easy-going world of rice fields, palm trees and rocky beaches, with excellent diving.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The bazaar and jetty
slots.text: Neil has a small bazaar and a sleepy jetty that leaps into action when ferries arrive.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Marina Beach
slots.text: One of the longest city beaches in the world, at 13km, with kite flyers, fortune tellers and beach cricket. Best early or late.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Fort St George
slots.venue: Fort St George & the Fort Museum
slots.text: The first British outpost in India, built after the East India Company bought the land in 1639, with a museum and St Mary's Church.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Madras Lighthouse
slots.text: A lift to the top gives views along the whole of Marina Beach. Late in the day gives the best photographs.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
slots.text: The temple that gave Mylapore its name, 'town of peacocks', with a 40m gopuram covered in painted deities.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: San Thome Cathedral
slots.text: Built on the reputed site of the Apostle Thomas's tomb, over a Portuguese basilica founded in 1523, with a small museum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Parthasarathy Temple
slots.text: A towering Triplicane temple founded in the 8th century, with shrines to five incarnations of Vishnu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Theosophical Society
slots.text: Free, tree-covered grounds holding a church, mosque, Hindu temple, Buddhist shrine and Zoroastrian fire altar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pondy Bazaar and T Nagar
slots.text: Silk saris, slippers, glass bangles and gold jewellery, with silks around Panagal Park. Expect big crowds.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Valluvar Kottam
slots.text: A memorial to the poet Thiruvalluvar, with a 31m stone temple chariot pulled by elephants. Entry costs three rupees.

days.title: The old town and Durbar Square

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The old town backstreets
slots.text: Walk from Thamel to Durbar Square past Kathesimbhu Stupa, Asan Tole, Indra Chowk and Itum Bahal, the city's largest courtyard.
slots.food: A glass of chiya, Nepali milk tea, along the way.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Durbar Square
slots.text: Malla-era temples and the Hanuman Dhoka palace. Budget half a day, and look in at the Kumari Bahal.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Thamel
slots.venue: Thamel: the buzz, and beyond it
slots.text: Global food all within two blocks, with Nepali craft beers from the Barasinghe and Sherpa breweries.
slots.food: Yin Yang for Thai, Third Eye for Indian, Utse for Tibetan.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Swayambhunath
slots.text: A 1,500-year-old white stupa on a hill with city views, and the monkeys that give it its nickname. Follow the kora at the base.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pashminas and thangkas
slots.text: Thamel's shops sell paper goods, silver jewellery and pashmina. For singing bowls and thangkas, go to Boudhanath.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Boudhanath
slots.text: Nepal's biggest Buddhist stupa, lit by hundreds of butter lamps at dusk while Tibetans circle it, spinning prayer wheels.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Patan Durbar Square
slots.venue: Patan Durbar Square & the Krishna Mandir
slots.text: A spectacular square of ornate temples and royal courtyards, plus the Patan Museum, Nepal's finest.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Patan's backstreets
slots.text: Spend a couple of hours among the Golden Temple and the four ancient stupas dating to the emperor Ashoka, and Patan's street art.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Newari food
slots.text: Patan is perhaps the best place to try traditional Newari food, such as wo, fried lentil pancakes.
slots.food: Choila, spiced barbecue meat, at Village Cafe or Raithaane.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Victoria Memorial
slots.text: The white marble 'Taj of the Raj', set in manicured gardens, with a museum of over 30,000 colonial-era artefacts. Closed Sundays.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Dalhousie Square
slots.text: Colonial Kolkata's heart: the Writers' Building, Raj Bhavan, High Court, General Post Office and Old Currency Building.
slots.food: Kathi rolls at Nizam's, a 100-year-old street stall.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Howrah Bridge and Prinsep Ghat
slots.text: Walk the riverfront at Prinsep Ghat for boat rides and views of Howrah Bridge, one of the longest cantilever bridges in the world.

days.title: A museum, a palace and a temple

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Indian Museum
slots.text: Founded in 1814, the oldest and largest museum in Asia-Pacific, with sculptures, Mughal paintings and mummies. Closed Mondays.
slots.food: Coffee at the Indian Coffee House.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Marble Palace
slots.text: Built in 1835 with Italian marble, with art, antiques and sculptures. Entry is free but needs permission from West Bengal Tourism.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dakshineshwar Kali Temple
slots.text: A revered temple on the Hooghly with a central shrine to Goddess Kali and 12 smaller shrines to Shiva.

days.title: Eden Gardens, street food and Park Street

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Eden Gardens
slots.text: India's oldest cricket stadium, from the 1860s. On non-match days you need permission from the Cricket Association of Bengal.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A street food trail
slots.text: Hubs include Park Street, New Market, College Street, Burrabazaar and Chinatown, with puchka at Vivekananda Park.
slots.food: Kachori and chola dal at Adi Haridas Modak, 250 years old.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Park Street
slots.text: Called the street that never sleeps, with clubs and live music venues such as Someplace Else and Tantra.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Ridge
slots.text: Home to Christ Church, the second oldest church in North India, with viewpoints over the mountains. No vehicles allowed.
slots.food: Breakfast at Wake and Bake on Mall Road.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mall Road
slots.text: A one-kilometre pedestrian street of restaurants, cafés and shops, including the famous Krishna Bakers and Trishool Bakers.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Gaiety Heritage Cultural Complex
slots.text: Built in 1887 on The Ridge, with regular plays, art exhibitions and events. Check the programme before you go.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gorton Castle
slots.text: A 1904 grey-stone castle with red roofs and Neo-Gothic towers, a gentle 20-minute walk from Mall Road. Free, closed Sundays.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Viceregal Lodge
slots.venue: The Viceregal Lodge (Indian Institute of Advanced Study)
slots.text: The 1880s summer residence of the Viceroy, in Jacobethan style. Entry is by 30-minute guided tour; closed Mondays.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Jakhu Temple and Ropeway
slots.text: Shimla's highest point, with a 108-foot Hanuman statue. The 5 to 6 minute ropeway gives a bird's-eye view of the town.
slots.food: Himachali thali at Cafe Khoblu or Himachali Rasoi.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Himachal State Museum
slots.text: In the Victorian mansion Inveram, with 17th-century miniature Pahari paintings and sculptures. Closed Mondays.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Annandale
slots.text: A small valley among deodar trees, with a golf course and the Army Heritage Museum. Free entry.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Brew Estate
slots.text: A local favourite for crafty cocktails and unique brews.
slots.food: Chinese and Tibetan dishes at the family-run Dim Sum.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The floating vegetable market
slots.venue: The Floating Vegetable Market at Dawn
slots.text: Take a shikara before sunrise to where vendors trade fruit, vegetables, flowers and walnut wood crafts from their boats.
slots.food: Czot bread for a floating breakfast, and kahwa from Mushtaq's shikara.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Hazratbal Shrine
slots.text: The shrine's dome watches over a market of vegetables and fabrics. Fridays have the best food.
slots.food: Fresh bread, giant puris with halwa, and spiced lentils.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A shikara to Char Chinar
slots.text: A pleasant evening in a shikara, visiting stops such as the island of four chinar trees, before dinner on the houseboat.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Shankaracharya Temple
slots.text: An ancient Shiva temple on a hill near Dal Lake, with breathtaking views of Srinagar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Mughal gardens
slots.text: Laid out on the Persian chaar-bagh plan, with flowers and fountains. Shalimar, Nishat and Chashme Shahi are all options.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Pari Mahal
slots.text: A 17th-century garden of seven terraces on the Zabarwan mountains, on the edge of Srinagar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Shah-e-Hamdan shrine
slots.text: Known for intricate woodwork and papier-mâché, in a part of town full of carpet weavers, coppersmiths and shawl makers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A wazwan lunch
slots.text: A celebratory meal of up to 36 dishes on Residency Road, at the century-old Ahdoos or the equally iconic Mughal Darbar.
slots.food: Wazwan, the Kashmiri feast.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Bund and Zero Bridge
slots.text: Polo View's market, the papier-mâché of Suffering Moses since 1840, then a walk along the Jhelum to the pedestrian Zero Bridge.
slots.food: Salty pink noon chai at Chai Jaai.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tiger's Nest
slots.text: A two-hour uphill hike north of Paro to a 1692 monastery that seems to grow from the cliff, 900m above the valley.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The National Museum
slots.text: A former watchtower, a museum since 1967, holding art, relics, thangka paintings and Bhutan's postage stamps.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Paro Dzong
slots.text: Light butter lamps, then cross the cantilever bridge for an evening view of the dzong and the museum.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dordenma Buddha
slots.text: A 51m bronze and steel statue with 125,000 smaller Buddhas inside, and views over the valley. Thimphu is 50km from Paro airport.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Takin Preserve and the market
slots.text: See the takin, Bhutan's national animal, from elevated walkways, then the Centenary Farmers Market with nearly 400 stalls.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Trashi Chho Dzong
slots.text: Arrive at 5pm as officials leave, to see the courtyards of Thimphu's most impressive building.
slots.food: Ema datse and jasha maroo at Chig Ja Gye.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Zorig Chusum
slots.text: The National Institute for Zorig Chusum, where students learn Bhutan's 13 traditional arts, from woodwork to embroidery.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Paper and weaving
slots.text: Watch paper made by hand at the Jungshi Handmade Paper Factory, and weaving at the Gagyel Lhundrup Weaving Centre.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Norzin Lam
slots.text: Thimphu's main street, just over a kilometre long, with cafés, a handicraft market of about 80 stalls and the traffic circle policeman.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Revi Karunakaran Memorial Museum
slots.text: A museum of Tanjore paintings, ivory and crystal, from a man known for his work in Kerala's coir industry. It closes by 2pm.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: St Mary's Forane Church
slots.text: One of the oldest Syrian Catholic churches in Kerala, on the River Pamba, with Portuguese influence and historical artefacts.
slots.food: Lunch at Hotel Brothers Restaurant or Choola Restaurant.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Alappuzha Beach
slots.venue: Alleppey Beach and the old pier
slots.text: Known worldwide for the Nehru Trophy Boat Race festivities, with an ancient lighthouse. A peaceful place to settle before dusk.
slots.food: Dinner at The Harbour Restaurant or Cassia.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A kayak or canoe tour
slots.text: Paddle creeks and canals too narrow for larger boats, past birdlife and waterside villages. Tours run three hours to a full day.
slots.food: A Kerala-style lunch comes with the full-day tours.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
slots.text: About 30 km from Alappuzha, home to rare birds including waterfowl, cuckoo, owl, teal and the Siberian crane.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Vembanad Lake sunset cruise
slots.text: Book a boat just before sunset on India's longest lake, 83.72 km long, as the colours change. Pathiramanal island is reached only by boat.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A kettuvallam cruise
slots.text: Drift past paddy fields, palm groves and Chinese-style cantilevered fishing nets on a traditional kettuvallam houseboat.
slots.food: Three meals a day cooked on board, and chai at sunrise.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A village stop
slots.text: Houseboat trips visit local villages to see traditional work such as fishing and toddy tapping.
slots.food: Try kallu, toddy, in a village toddy shop.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sunset on the backwaters
slots.text: Fiery sunsets over the water, then a night to the sound of insects. The classic overnight trip from Alleppey.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tiger Hill sunrise
slots.text: A convoy of 4WDs climbs before dawn to a view of Khangchendzonga turning pink, with Everest beyond. Wrap up warm.
slots.food: Chai-wallahs serve hot tea to the crowd.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Toy Train
slots.venue: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway Toy Train Joy Ride
slots.text: Steam locomotives still run from Darjeeling to Ghum and back, past tea gardens, on the narrow-gauge railway begun in 1879.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Peace Pagoda
slots.text: A 28m white Japanese pagoda. Arrive at about 4:15pm to join a drumming puja in the temple below, which lasts up to 90 minutes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Happy Valley Tea Estate
slots.text: Tours of the estate and factory end with a tasting of all four flushes. Come between late March and mid-November, Tuesday to Saturday.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tibetan Refugee Self-Help Centre
slots.text: Workshops for painting, textiles and woodworking, a small monastery and a shop, on the ridge below Chowrasta.
slots.food: Tea tastings at Nathmulls, which showcases more than 50 teas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Momos and thukpa
slots.text: Tibetan food came with the refugees. Kunga on Gandhi Road is a National Geographic pick for the best momo dumplings.
slots.food: Thukpa noodle soup at Noryang Tibetan Kitchen, where the noodles are made by hand.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Observatory Hill
slots.text: A hilltop above Chowrasta shared by Hindus and Buddhists, with prayer flags, bells and cheeky rhesus macaques.
slots.food: Breakfast at tiny Sonam's Kitchen on Dr Zakir Hussain Road.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Himalayan Mountaineering Institute
slots.text: The history of Himalayan expeditions, with a statue and samadhi shrine of Tenzing Norgay in the grounds of the zoological park.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: High tea at the Windamere
slots.text: A cluster of cottages from the British Raj, with vintage furnishings, offering high tea to non-guests and views of the high Himalaya.

days.title: A museum, a haunted village and the lake

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jaisalmer Government Museum
slots.text: Artefacts from the seventh and ninth centuries AD, including a trophy of the state bird, the Godawan, plus jewellery and crockery. Closed Fridays.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kuldhara
slots.text: A village a few kilometres out, said to be haunted. Legend says its people left overnight in the 1800s. Golden-hued homes and an eerie charm.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Gadisar Lake
slots.text: Once the city's only water reservoir. Watch the sunset, go boating or catch the Laser Water Show. Entry is free.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jaisalmer Fort
slots.text: Built in 1156 and still lived in, with 99 bastions and four gates. Allow three to four hours. Entry is INR 50 for Indians.
slots.food: Buy umbrellas and dupattas inside, and bargain well.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jain temples and the palace
slots.text: The fort's Jain temples, the Raj Mahal and the Queen's palace, with a bird's-eye view of the city from the top.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The local markets
slots.text: Manak Chowk, Pansari Bazar and Sonaron Ka Bazar sell leheriya and bandhani clothes, turbans, pickles and handmade wares.
slots.food: Dal baati churma, pyaaz ki kachori and makhania lassi.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The havelis
slots.text: A five-storey Patwon Ki Haveli with carvings and mirror work, half a kilometre from the fort. Salim Singh and Nathmal Ji havelis are a five-minute walk.
slots.food: Gatte ki sabzi and ker sangri for lunch.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Desert National Park
slots.text: Jeep safaris go in search of the Great Indian Bustard, eagles, falcons, desert fox, chinkara and desert cat.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sam sunset
slots.text: Magnificent sunset views at Sam village, where you can stay at a safari camp among the sand dunes, or head back to your hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Mehrangarh Fort
slots.text: Rajasthan's biggest fort, built in 1459 on a cliff 400 feet above the city, with a museum of miniature paintings, palanquins and arms.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jaswant Thada
slots.text: A cenotaph from 1899, built entirely of thin, carved marble sheets that glow in the sun, with a tiered garden and a small lake.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Clock Tower market
slots.text: The Sardar Market around the Ghantaghar sells mojaris, lehariya saris, dupattas, safas and ethnic jewellery.
slots.food: Piping hot pyaz kachoris and mirchi vadas.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Flying Fox zipline
slots.text: A zipline over two desert lakes and the Rao Jodha eco-park, with views of Mehrangarh and the Blue City.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mandore Garden
slots.text: Ancient temples, memorials and high-rock terraces, with monoliths from the fifth century and a government museum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Umaid Bhawan Palace
slots.text: An Indo-Saracenic palace of interlocked sandstone, with no mortar. Part is a hotel; part shows model aeroplanes, clocks and crockery.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Osian's temples
slots.text: About 65 km from Jodhpur, a town called the Khajuraho of Rajasthan, with 8th to 12th century temples. Go early.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The dunes
slots.text: Osian's own crowd-free sand dunes, for a stroll or a camel or jeep safari, which can take 3 to 6 hours.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A desert camp
slots.text: Sit on the dunes for sunset. Overnight camps have folk dances, bonfires and stargazing, or return to Jodhpur.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A Fort Kochi walk
slots.text: On foot from Fort Immanuel to St Francis Church, where Vasco da Gama was once laid to rest, the Dutch Cemetery and Santa Cruz Basilica.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kashi Art Café
slots.text: In a century-old Dutch colonial structure, an art gallery and café with a shaded courtyard.
slots.food: Home-baked cakes, French toast and strong organic coffee.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Chinese fishing nets
slots.text: Swaying against the Arabian Sea at Vasco da Gama Square, they are at their most magical at sunset.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Mattancherry Palace
slots.text: Gifted by the Portuguese to King Veera Kerala Varma in 1555 and restored by the Dutch, hence the Dutch Palace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Paradesi Synagogue and Jew Town
slots.text: Built in 1568, with hand-painted Chinese tiles and Belgian chandeliers, and lanes of antique shops and spice shops.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kerala Kathakali Centre
slots.text: The most popular venue in Fort Kochi for Kathakali, Mohiniattam and the martial art Kalaripayattu.
slots.food: Dinner at Malabar Junction: fish pollichathu and payasam.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hill Palace
slots.text: Built in 1865 for the Cochin kings in Tripunithura, now Kerala's largest archaeological museum.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The backwaters by ferry
slots.text: Ferries have linked Kochi's ten inhabited islands since 1968. The new Kochi Water Metro runs electric hybrid boats.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Rice Boat
slots.text: Styled as a kettuvalam, in the Taj Malabar on Willingdon Island, with views of the backwaters and Mattancherry.
slots.food: Tiger prawns in coconut oil and white snapper in banana leaf.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Victoria
slots.text: One of the world's smallest capitals, below a mountain landscape of banana plants and palms, with a market and a silver clock tower inspired by Big Ben.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Beau Vallon Beach
slots.text: Mahé's hub for motorised water sports and seaside fun, on the north-west coast.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Beach Shak
slots.text: An open-air bar right on the sand with a west-facing view for the sunset. Book ahead.
slots.food: Try a Creole Rhum Swizzle: extra dark rum, Creole bitters and cinnamon syrup.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Morne Seychellois National Park
slots.text: 7,525 acres of mountain jungle and mangroves, 20% of Mahé, with over nine miles of trails to the Seychelles' highest point.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jardin du Roi
slots.text: A spice garden high above the coast, where the restaurant serves curries made with fresh herbs from the grounds.
slots.food: A farm-to-table lunch.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Takamaka Rum Distillery
slots.venue: Takamaka Rum Distillery, La Plaine St André
slots.text: A restored plantation house, La Plaine St André, with a guided tour of the stills and a tasting.
slots.food: A drink and a bite at the Rum Shack and Food Truck.

days.title: Fruit, glass-bottom boats and Creole dinner

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Vallée des Fruits
slots.text: Seychelles' first organic fruit agrotourism experience: a plantation tour among mango, guava and passionfruit trees.
slots.food: Sample FruitShi, fruit served sushi-style, or join a Creole cooking session.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Moyenne Island
slots.text: A glass-bottom boat shows corals, sea meadows and schools of fish. Eden Island's semi-submarine is another way to see the reef.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Marie Antoinette
slots.text: Authentic Creole dining in Victoria, in a 150-year-old colonial-era mansion that holds the charm of old Seychelles.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hadimba Temple
slots.text: A four-tiered pagoda temple from 1553 set among the cedars of Dhungri forest, dedicated to Goddess Hadimba, with ancient wooden architecture and intricate carvings.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Old Manali and Manu Temple
slots.text: Wander Old Manali's bohemian lanes along the Beas River, full of shops and cosy cafes, up to Manu Temple dedicated to the sage Manu.
slots.food: Sip hot chai or share Maggi noodles at a cafe like 1947 or Dylan's.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Mall Road
slots.text: Stroll the town's main promenade, lined with local shops and Tibetan handicrafts; good for Pashmina shawls, woollen caps and the iconic Himachali topi.
slots.food: Grab warm momos and a softy as you walk Mall Road.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Solang Valley
slots.text: A short drive from town, this valley of snow-capped peaks and green meadows is Manali's adventure hub, with skiing, paragliding, zorbing and a 1.5-km cable car ride.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rohtang Pass
slots.text: At 13,000 feet, one of India's most famous mountain passes, with sweeping Himalayan views; the drive passes the Atal Tunnel toward Spiti. A permit is needed and it opens June to September.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Vashisht hot springs
slots.text: Unwind in the natural sulphur hot springs of this hillside hamlet an hour from town, beside wooden temples and mountains, the perfect end to a day in the snow.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jogini Waterfalls
slots.text: A serene one-to-two-hour hike through dense forest and streams leads to these rejuvenating falls above Vashisht, a favourite of nature lovers and adventurers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Naggar Castle
slots.text: A 30-minute drive to the old Kullu capital, where a 15th-century stone-and-wood castle and the Nicholas Roerich art gallery sit against snow-capped peaks.
slots.food: Enjoy a royal lunch with valley views at Naggar Castle.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Old Manali cafes
slots.text: Close the trip in Old Manali's buzzing cafe-and-bar scene, where spots like Cafe 1947 and The Lazy Dog Lounge host live music by the river.
slots.food: Woodfired pizza or a hearty mountain meal with live tunes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tea Museum
slots.text: A 1.5-km walk north-west of town, the closest thing to a working tea factory: colonial-era exhibits, a 1905 tea-roller and a 30-minute film on Munnar's tea history.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Walk the tea estates
slots.text: Whether or not you love tea, a walk through the plantations is essential; the climate, the aroma and the quiet are breathtaking.
slots.food: Refuel on parathas and biryani at Raspy Restaurant, a local favourite.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Punarjani Traditional Village
slots.text: About 8 km south of town, watch enchanting daily Kathakali (5pm) and Kalari (6pm) performances; arrive by 4pm to catch the ritual Kathakali makeup sessions.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Eravikulam National Park
slots.text: Set among rolling hills, this park is the best place near Munnar to meet the endangered Nilgiri Tahr, a shy mountain goat, in the wild.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Echo Point
slots.text: A lakeside spot ringed by green hills where your loudest yell echoes back across the water, a fun, scenic stop that brings out the child in everyone.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner in town
slots.text: Head back into Munnar for dinner at a bright, modern eatery like Surya Soma, playing upbeat tunes over a welcoming dining room.
slots.food: Affordable North Indian, local and Chinese dishes.

days.title: Flowers, a lake and Keralan cooking

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Blossom International Flower Park
slots.text: Sixteen acres of flowers to wander, with boating, cycling and even roller-blading when you need a break from the blooms.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sita Devi Lake
slots.text: A pretty hill lake where, unusually for a hill station, you can sit and fish to your heart's content amid Munnar's green diversity.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Keralan cooking class
slots.text: Learn authentic Keralan recipes at blogger Nimi Sunilkumar's daily cooking class near the DTPC; you leave with a copy of her cookbook.
slots.food: A hands-on Keralan supper you cook yourself.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Settle in
slots.text: The park is over three hours from Jaipur airport, so arrive, settle into your lodge and rest; the wild days ahead begin in earnest tomorrow.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Afternoon jeep safari
slots.text: Board a jeep or canter for a three-hour safari into zones one to five, the oldest and best-maintained, where tigers roam unhindered by the cameras.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Oberoi Vanyavilas
slots.text: Unwind with open-air yoga and wellness therapies after the dust of the trail at this resort, a ten-minute drive from the gate for zones one to five.

days.title: Dawn and dusk in the core zones

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Padam Talao
slots.text: The park's largest lake, where tigers and sambar gather at the water's edge and the red-sandstone Jogi Mahal stands on the bank, a classic morning sighting spot.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ranthambore Fort
slots.text: A 10th-century fort standing in the middle of the forest; climb for sweeping views and old temples, and you may spot a tiger on the way up.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Evening jeep safari
slots.text: Take a second safari into the core zones at dusk; your guide knows where tigresses have laid cubs and where males are fighting over territory.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Chambal boat safari
slots.text: Swap the jeep for a boat on the River Chambal that rings the park, spotting gharials, alligators and birds like pintails, egrets, herons, storks and flamingos.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Keoladeo detour
slots.text: On the way out, detour to this UNESCO-listed bird sanctuary near Bharatpur, one of the world's great breeding grounds for waterfowl, spoonbills and storks.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Drive to Jaipur
slots.text: It is about three hours back to Jaipur airport, so keep buffer time before your flight after a wild few days in the jungle.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Yoga by the Ganges
slots.text: In the 'Yoga Capital of the World', start with a riverside drop-in class at an ashram like Parmarth Niketan, stretching against a Himalayan backdrop.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Beatles Ashram
slots.text: Explore the graffiti-covered ruins of the Maharishi Mahesh Yogi Ashram where the Beatles once stayed, now a gallery of vivid street art among the trees.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat
slots.venue: The Maha Aarti at Triveni Ghat
slots.text: Arrive 30 to 45 minutes early for the 6pm Ganga Aarti: incense, bells and chanting as priests offer prayers to the river and lamps shimmer on the water.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: White-water rafting
slots.text: Raft the Ganga's mix of calm stretches and Grade I to V rapids; popular put-ins run from Brahmpuri and Shivpuri down to Marine Drive and Kaudiyala.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bungee at Jumpin Heights
slots.text: For a bigger rush, take the leap at Jumpin Heights, an 80-metre bungee certified by the Ministry of Tourism; Himalayan Bungy nearby goes to 117 metres.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Riverside cafe
slots.text: Wind down at a riverside cafe like the Beatles Cafe or Shambala, watching the Ganges slip past as the town's nightlife hums to life.
slots.food: Wood-fired pizza and coffee with a Ganges view.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
slots.text: A hilltop Shiva temple some 5,000 feet up, reached by a 45-minute drive or a 12-km trek, where legend says Shiva drank the poison that turned his throat blue.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Laxman Jhula and markets
slots.venue: Lakshman Jhula & Ram Jhula (the swaying footbridges)
slots.text: Cross the famous suspension bridge over the Ganga and browse the lanes for Rudraksha beads, incense and bohemian souvenirs.
slots.food: Taste aloo poori and kachori with a glass of chilled lassi.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Vashishta Gufa
slots.text: Meditate in this ancient cave where Sage Vashishta is said to have sat for years; bring a torch, as the long cave is dark and quiet.

days.title: The city palace and the lake

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: City Palace
slots.text: Spend two or three hours in the sprawling lakeside palace complex, taking in Mewar architecture, courtyards and heritage galleries above Lake Pichola.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Boating on Lake Pichola
slots.venue: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
slots.text: Take a 30-minute boat ride on the lake, then walk among the lakeside pavilions; the water frames the City Palace and its island palaces.
slots.food: Lunch at Ambrai, the city's most Instagrammed lakefront restaurant.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sunset at Karni Mata Temple
slots.venue: Karni Mata ropeway to Machla Magra
slots.text: Ride the ropeway up to this hilltop temple, perched on Machla Magra, for the city's most picturesque sunset over the lakes and palaces below.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Saheliyon ki Bari
slots.text: Spend an hour or two in this royal fountain garden of lotus pools, marble elephants and flowerbeds, built for the ladies of the court.
slots.food: Stop at The Bake Affair Cafe nearby for great coffee and eggless patisserie.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Vintage and Classic Car Museum
slots.text: See the Mewar dynasty's collection of classic cars, from grand Rolls-Royces to Cadillacs, many of them still in working order.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Palasa Patio Bar
slots.text: Escape the tourist throng at this hidden outdoor bar in leafy Shikarbadi, 30 minutes out, with alcove seating and an eclectic Western menu.
slots.food: Tapas-style bites and standout G&Ts.

days.title: Lake, art and a sunset fort

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Fateh Sagar Lake
slots.text: Boat on this hill-ringed lake before the sun is overhead; it holds three small islands and is a calmer counterpart to Lake Pichola.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rajasthan Studio
slots.text: Spend two hours learning 16th-century miniature painting with master artist Kanhaiya Sharma, creating your own little souvenir to take home.
slots.food: Lunch at Kaner Bistro Lounge, an all-veg cafe in a leafy haveli courtyard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sunset at Sajjangarh
slots.text: Close the trip with sunset from this hilltop fort, also called the Monsoon Palace, looking out over Udaipur's lakes and the city below.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Assi Ghat at dawn
slots.text: Rickshaw to Assi Ghat before dawn for the 45-minute Subah-e-Banaras aarti, shloka chanting and sunrise yoga where the Ganga meets the Assi.
slots.food: Breakfast at Brown Bread Bakery, with organic and vegan options.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Shivala Ghat and BHU
slots.text: Stroll to Shivala and Shankaracharya Ghat for a 15-minute boat ride, then visit Banaras Hindu University's Indo-Gothic campus and Bharat Kala Bhavan museum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dashashwamedh Ghat
slots.venue: The Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
slots.text: Around 5pm, take a boat out to watch the elaborate evening Ganga aarti, with priests moving in unison, then a fire-dance ritual and prayers.
slots.food: Try the best-selling tamatar chaat at Kashi Chat Bhandar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
slots.text: Take a rickshaw to Vishwanath Gali for one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines, with ornate carvings and black-stone lingams.
slots.food: Start with idlis, masala dosa and filter coffee at Kerala Cafe near Bhelupur Road.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Man Singh Observatory
slots.venue: Man Mandir Ghat & the Man Singh Observatory (Jantar Mantar)
slots.text: Climb the observatory built in 1710 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh for panoramic views of the Ganges' west bank.
slots.food: Pehalwan Lassi in a kulhad near Ravidas Gate, then a Banarasi paan at Keshav Bhandar.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dhamekh Stupa at sunset
slots.text: Take a taxi to Sarnath, where Buddha gave his first sermon, to watch the sun set behind this 43-metre Buddhist shrine dating back to 500 CE.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dawn boat on the Ganges
slots.venue: A Dawn Boat Ride on the Ganga
slots.text: Hire a boat at dawn to watch devotees bathe and perform puja, yogis salute the sun and hawkers greet the crowds as the city lights up from the water.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Walk to Manikarnika Ghat
slots.text: Walk the 3 km of ghats past temples, boatmen and bathers to Manikarnika, one of the burning ghats where pyres burn around the clock.
slots.food: Stop for a fresh fruit lassi at Blue Lassi, churning 80 flavours since 1925.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Gaudoliya Street Market
slots.text: Browse some of the city's oldest shops near Varanasi Cantt station for Banarasi sarees and handwoven carpets; Thatheri Bazar and Golghar are alternatives.
slots.food: Finish with dal bati and bowls of kheer at Baati Chokha.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Stone Town heritage walk
slots.text: Wander the UNESCO-listed coralline ragstone streets with a local guide, past carved doors and shops scented with vanilla and cloves.
slots.food: Pick up an invigorating cup of spiced coffee along the way.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The church on the old slave market
slots.venue: The Anglican Cathedral & the former Slave Market
slots.text: A historic church stands on what was once East Africa's largest market of enslaved people, a sobering stop in the heart of the old town.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Forodhani Gardens
slots.text: Watch the sunset over the ocean from these waterfront gardens, the perfect finish to a day on foot in Stone Town.
slots.food: Taste a meat-stuffed sambusa as the sun goes down.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Matemwe village and fish auction
slots.text: Walk with a guide to the nearby fishing village and its fish auction, a lively look at daily life on the island's northeast coast.
slots.food: Sample biscuit-like Swahili doughnuts.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Matemwe Lodge lagoon
slots.text: Watch dhows sail over the coral-reef lagoon from a hammock, as fisherpeople walk far out to sea when the tide ebbs more than half a mile.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dinner at LUX* Marijani
slots.text: Opened in 2023 on the northeast coast, this whitewashed hotel puts clove, cinnamon and nutmeg at the heart of its two restaurants.
slots.food: Try the aromatic octopus curry at The Beach, or vegetarian sharing plates at Samāa.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jambiani Beach
slots.text: On the southwest coast, the family-run Blue Oyster Hotel is a mainstay of this beach and gives local masseuses and craftswomen space on site.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kendwa Beach
slots.text: On the northwest coast, thatch-roofed suites and villas sit among tropical gardens along the sand, blending quietly into the landscape.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Emerson Spice
slots.text: Dine on the rooftop of a restored merchant's house in Stone Town, where indigenous ingredients take centre stage and local musicians perform.
